target.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes MCP server loading failure when tools have `inputSchema` without explicit `type: "object"`.

Closes #63602

## Changes
- `listAllTools` validates each `tools/list` page **once** with `RelaxedListToolsResultSchema` and catalogs **that same validated payload** — there is no strict-then-relist flow, so a stateful or hostile server cannot pass validation with one response and have a different response consumed (no validation-to-use gap).
- `RelaxedToolSchema` is **derived from the pinned SDK's own `ToolSchema`** (`ToolSchema.extend` / `ToolSchema.shape.inputSchema.extend`) and differs from it at exactly one point: the root `inputSchema.type` is an optional string instead of `z.literal("object")`. Every other field — `outputSchema`, task `execution` metadata, `annotations`, pagination — keeps the exact pinned SDK contract, so malformed metadata still rejects the page.
- After every page parse, the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` is invoked with the validated tools — the same side effect `client.listTools()` runs — so `callTool()` enforces output-schema validation and task-required guards identically to the SDK flow. The call is optional (no crash if a future SDK removes the method) and a dedicated test pins the method's existence so a dependency upgrade that drops it fails loudly rather than silently shedding the guards.
- `normalizeInputSchema()` backfills `type: "object"` only when the field is missing; `isValidRootInputSchema()` + the catalog gate skip tools with an explicit non-object root type (e.g. `"string"`, `"array"`) with a `logWarn`. Server `toolCount` reports accepted tools only.

## Root Cause
The MCP SDK v1.29.0 `ToolSchema` validates `inputSchema.type` as `z.literal("object")`. Some MCP servers (especially older SDKs or custom implementations) omit `type` from `inputSchema`, returning `{ properties: { ... } }`, which trips a Zod validation error: `invalid_value expected "object" in inputSchema.type` and crashes the whole catalog.

## v6 notes (current revision)
Addresses the P1 from the latest review (validation-to-use gap, confidence 0.96) by adopting its recommended repair: single-response validation that differs from the pinned SDK `ToolSchema` only at the root `inputSchema.type`, with SDK-equivalent metadata caching, explicit non-object filtering, and pagination preserved.
- The strict-then-relist flow is gone entirely; the request count per page is 1 in all cases.
- New stateful-server regression: a server that returns a benign typeless payload on request 1 and a malicious payload on request 2 gets exactly one `tools/list` request, and only the validated payload is cataloged. **Mutation-checked**: against the previous strict-then-relist implementation this test fails with the catalog containing the drifted (never-strictly-validated) tool — reproducing the reported attack — and the server log showing two list requests.
- New SDK-seam pin test: `Client.prototype.cacheToolMetadata` must exist, making the documented private-method dependency an explicit, loudly-failing audit point on SDK upgrades (P1 risk #2 from the same review).
- Relaxation-scope unit tests: malformed `outputSchema`, malformed `execution.taskSupport`, and missing `inputSchema` all still reject the page; pagination (`nextCursor`) keeps the SDK contract.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior or issue addressed: Bundle MCP tool cataloging accepts tools whose root `inputSchema` omits `type` by validating each `tools/list` response once against a schema derived from the pinned SDK contract (relaxed only at the root `inputSchema.type`), backfills `type: "object"`, skips explicit non-object roots, keeps servers with unrelated strict failures rejected, never issues a second list request, and preserves the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` side effects for every page.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS from the rebased PR head, Node 25.2.1, pnpm 11.2.2, driving the real bundle MCP runtime (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` → `getCatalog()` → `callTool()`) against four real out-of-process stdio MCP servers, one of them stateful (different payload per request).

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran `pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on both files, plus a live four-server e2e script via `pnpm exec tsx`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  42 passed (42)
pnpm tsgo:core / tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint / oxfmt --check: clean

e2e (four live stdio servers):
tools: ["legacySdkServer/search_docs","driftServer/benign_typeless_tool"]
servers: {"legacySdkServer":{"toolCount":1},"driftServer":{"toolCount":1}}
rejected: ["badOutputServer","mixedServer"]
driftServer tools/list requests received: 1        // exactly one — no second-request window
callTool(search_docs) → McpError -32600: Tool search_docs has an output schema but did not
  return structured content                        // metadata cache populated from the same response
```

Observed result after fix: A `tools/list` payload whose `inputSchema` omits `type` catalogs cleanly with `type: "object"` backfilled; an explicit `type: "array"` sibling is skipped with a logWarn; servers with malformed `outputSchema` (alone or mixed with a repairable tool) stay rejected; a stateful server attempting response drift receives exactly one list request and only its validated payload is cataloged; `callTool()` enforces `outputSchema` for typeless tools exactly as the SDK strict flow would.

What was not tested: A live third-party MCP server connected to an actual model-provider tool call was not tested in this environment.

## What Problem This Solves

When the Telegram Mini App page receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 401 auth error), the response body stream is left dangling without being cancelled. This can leak connections and waste resources in the Mini App's WebView environment.

**Root Cause**: The `renderTelegramMiniAppPage()` function's `fetch("auth", ...)` handler was missing `response.body?.cancel()` before `throw new Error("auth failed")`, leaving the response body stream unread and un-cancelled on auth errors.

**Solution**: Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw, matching the established codebase pattern used across `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and other extensions.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Local HTTP server simulating Telegram auth endpoint (401 response), Node.js `fetch` API.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```

 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 500: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 429: body cancelled 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 503: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Null body: safe (no error on missing body) 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Cancel rejection: suppressed 1ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
All non-2xx paths call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing, verified across status codes 400, 403, 429, 500, 503. Null body and cancellation rejection edge cases are also handled.

**What was not tested**:
`postJson` was not modified — it reads the error response body via `response.json()` to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### Fix 2: Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:

Malformed JSON at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` now produces `Error("Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: /path/to/file")` instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. The `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` caller catches this and returns `undefined`, so `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` degrades gracefully instead of crashing.

The fix is in `readGoogleAdcCredentials` which is called from two paths: (a) `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` used by `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync`, and (b) `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders`. Both paths are covered: (a) via the integration test above, and (b) via the error-recovery path — if credentials are invalid, the function throws, which is caught upstream and falls through to `google-auth-library`.

## Tests and validation

target.title: fix(doctor): guard snapshot store load against corrupt JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` had a broad catch that silently swallowed all errors from corrupt JSON or unreadable snapshot stores, returning `{}`. This prevented the caller from diagnosing the failure — a corrupt store was indistinguishable from an empty one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inner try/catch merged two distinct failure modes (corrupt JSON, unreadable file) into a silent empty result. The caller `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` already had a catch boundary, but it was dead code because the inner function never threw. This fix:
1. Removes the inner catch so JSON parse / filesystem errors propagate naturally
2. The caller catch at `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` now handles the error instead of being dead code

Now a corrupt or unreadable snapshot store produces a visible diagnostic while continuing to scan other stores.

## User Impact

Prevents silent skipping of corrupt snapshot stores during `openclaw doctor` session snapshot health checks. The user now sees a clear diagnostic when a store cannot be loaded.

## Evidence

## Summary

`loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` fetches the `debug/requests` endpoint from a configured QA Lab runtime parity server. When the endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status (503, 400, 500), the function returns null early without consuming the response body stream, leaving an unread stream resource dangling that may hold the connection open.

The fix adds `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the early return on `!response.ok`. This cancels the unread body stream, matching the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path.

**What changed**: One line added in `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` at `runtime-parity.ts:1055`. No changes to the ok path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the ok response path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality. No new dependencies or configuration options added.

Fixes #109991

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` returns null early on non-ok HTTP responses without cancelling the unread response body stream, potentially leaking resources and holding connections open.

**Root Cause**: At `runtime-parity.ts:1055`, the `!response.ok` early-return path calls `return null` without first cancelling the response body stream via `response.body?.cancel()`. The ok path implicitly drains the body via `response.json()`, but the non-ok path has no such cleanup.

**Solution**: Add `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before returning null on non-ok responses. This mirrors the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path. The `.catch(() => undefined)` guard ensures safety even if the body stream is already in an inconsistent state.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Body cancel on non-ok HTTP response in QA Lab runtime parity mock tool-call fetch path.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic / Node.js 22 / OpenClaw 2026.7.2 / HTTP mock server (127.0.0.1) exercising `captureRuntimeParityCell` with non-ok debug/requests endpoint responses.

target.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running browser screenshot with a configured image-understanding model would have the session become unusable when that vision model failed: later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` tool results were framed as image analysis until `/new`.

The vision-failure path previously fell back to injecting a raw base64 image block into the tool result. That image-bearing result is retained across recent completed turns, so it keeps re-entering model context and contaminates subsequent tool use.

This is the failure path described in #106703 (and the same root cause reported in #105305).

## Why This Change Was Made

The vision success path already returns a text-only description. This change makes the configured-vision failure path consistent with it: on describe failure, return a text-only result that reports the failure reason and keeps the staged outbound-copy path so the screenshot can still be shared explicitly via the message tool. Never write base64 image data into session/tool-result state on that path.

Scoped intentionally:

- Configured vision model throws: text-only (fixed path). A user who configured image understanding opted into text descriptions, so a transient provider error should not silently switch to dumping raw base64.
- Image understanding skipped / not configured (`describeBrowserScreenshot` returns `null`): still returns the raw image, so vision-capable primary models that rely on seeing the screenshot are unaffected.

## User Impact

When a configured image-understanding model fails during browser screenshot, the session stays usable: tool results remain text-framed, and the screenshot can still be shared via the message tool. Users without image understanding configured keep the previous model-visible screenshot behavior.

## Evidence

### Real-handler behavioral proof

The reported symptom is a session-state effect: on a configured image-understanding failure the screenshot tool result previously carried a raw base64 image block, which is retained across recent completed turns (`pruneProcessedHistoryImages` keeps image blocks from the last `PRESERVE_RECENT_COMPLETED_TURNS = 3` completed turns) and forces later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` results into image-analysis framing until `/new`.

The proof drives the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot handler with the configured image-understanding call (`describeImageFile`) forced to fail, then drives a later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler. Only the vision call is mocked (to throw); the screenshot handler, its catch path, and the surrounding tool flow are real production code. It lives in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` under the describe block `browser screenshot vision-failure session-contamination proof (#106703, #105305)`.

Reproduce:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts --disableConsoleIntercept
```

Redacted transcript (content-block types and image-block counts only; no base64 bytes are printed):

```
--- real screenshot handler (configured vision failure) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: [browser screenshot vision failed: vision provider unavailable (HTTP 503)] \n [Screenshot saved to "/tmp/openclaw-media/outbound/share.png". Use this path with the message tool to share the screenshot explicitly.]
--- real snapshot handler (later tool call) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: <<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT source="browser">>> \n ok \n <<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT>>>
=== session transcript (redacted) ===
user: screenshot the dashboard and summarize it
toolResult(browser:screenshot): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: the configured vision model was unavailable
user: now read the deploy status file
toolResult(read): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: deploy is green
user: take a page snapshot
toolResult(browser:snapshot): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: captured snapshot
total image content blocks across session: 0
--- no-vision path (unchanged) screenshot result ---
content-block types: [text, image]
image content blocks: 1
text: browser:screenshot
```

Reading the transcript:

- Real screenshot handler with configured vision forced to fail: the emitted tool result is text-only (`image content blocks: 0`), carries the neutralized failure reason and the staged outbound-copy share hint, and sets `details.vision.failed` with no `details.media`.
- A later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler stays text-framed, and the reconstructed multi-turn session carries `total image content blocks: 0`, so nothing base64 rides alongside later `read` / `snapshot` results.
- No-vision path (unchanged): the same handler still reaches `imageResultFromFile` and emits a base64 image block (`image content blocks: 1`). This is the exact tool-result shape the pre-fix catch produced and that `pruneProcessedHistoryImages` preserves for recent turns, so the mechanism is real and the fix is scoped to the configured-vision-failure catch.

Honesty note on scope: this environment could not stand up a fully-live browser node plus a real failing vision provider end to end, so the single vision call is mocked to throw at its real boundary. Everything else (the screenshot handler, its catch path, the later snapshot handler, and the neutralization plus share-staging wrapping) is real production code, and the emitted tool-result shapes above are what the handler actually returns.

### Handler-side unit and regression tests

Focused tests in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` drive the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot path:

- `defangs vision failure fallback text and stays text-only`: vision-failure result is text-only (no `imageResultFromFile`, no image content block, no `details.media`) while preserving the neutralized failure text and share hint.
- `never injects a raw image block when configured vision fails (#106703, #105305)`: configured-vision failure returns zero image content blocks and marks `details.vision.failed`, so the result cannot persist an image across turns.
- No-vision (skipped/unconfigured) path still returns the raw image with sanitization.

### Local gate (redacted)

```

vitest extensions/browser/src/browser/vision.test.ts                          6 passed
vitest src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/history-image-prune.test.ts      12 passed
lint:extensions                                                             clean
format:check                                                                clean
tsgo:extensions:test                                                        0 errors
deadcode:full (knip production + all-exports)                               clean  (resolves check-dependencies unused-file)
```

target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

Boot-echo guard chunking used `String.prototype.slice()` which operates on UTF-16 code units and can split surrogate pairs (emoji, CJK beyond BMP, etc.), producing malformed chunks. This caused the substantial-echo comparison to miss matches when the alignment boundary falls inside a surrogate pair. Replace `.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` to preserve surrogate pair integrity during chunk extraction.

What changed: `getBootPromptChunks` and `containsSubstantialBootEcho` now use `sliceUtf16Safe()` from normalization-core instead of `String.prototype.slice()`. What did NOT change: algorithm, chunking logic, cache structure, public API, or behavior for ASCII/BMP-only text.

Fixes #110641

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The boot-echo guard fails to detect echoes when the boot prompt or outbound text contains characters outside the BMP (surrogate pairs), because `String.prototype.slice()` can split a surrogate pair and produce an invalid UTF-16 string that won't match the corresponding chunk.

**Root Cause**: In `src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.ts`, both `getBootPromptChunks()` and `containsSubstantialBootEcho()` used `.slice()` to extract comparison substrings. `String.prototype.slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when a boundary falls inside a surrogate pair, the resulting string is malformed.

**Solution**: Replace `String.prototype.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. A helper `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen()` wraps the safe slice to maintain the minimum chunk length invariant.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**: All 6 boot-echo guard tests pass on current HEAD.

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

## Tests and validation

All 6 existing unit tests pass, confirming the UTF-16 safe chunking doesn't regress ASCII/BMP behavior.

## What Problem This Solves
WhatsApp group agents currently have two practical modes: wake only on each mention, or wake on every message with `/activation always`. In real group conversations, users often mention the agent once and then continue with follow-up messages without repeating the mention, so the agent misses the rest of the short exchange unless the owner switches the whole group to always-on.

This PR adds an opt-in middle ground for allowed WhatsApp groups: a temporary listen window after a valid mention. It keeps the existing group allowlist and sender authorization gates intact, and only relaxes mention gating for the same account, agent, session, and group JID while the window is active.

- add `listenAfterMentionMs` and `listenAfterMentionMaxMs` per WhatsApp group entry
- admit follow-up messages during the configured window and extend up to the configured cap
- clear the active window on `/activation mention` without reopening it from the command turn
- document the behavior and add focused tests for admission, cap expiry, command clearing, and schema parsing

target.title: fix(reef): contain startup friend reconcile failures
target.body:
Related: #110870

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running the Reef channel against a relay that is rate limiting would see Reef stop permanently and stay down until the process was restarted by hand, instead of riding out the throttling and recovering on its own.

While the relay returns 429, starting the Reef account fails outright. The gateway supervisor restarts it, each restart hits the same throttled relay again, and after ten attempts Reef gives up for the lifetime of the process — logging `giving up after 10 restart attempts`. Because every attempt issues another relay request, the restart cycle also feeds the throttling that caused it.

#110870 fixed exactly this amplifier for the periodic reconcile that runs every 30s, but the reconcile that runs once at account startup was not covered by that change and still fails the whole account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup and periodic reconcile are the same relay call with two different failure policies: the periodic one reports the error and keeps the channel alive, the startup one rejects `startAccount`. This change gives them one shared policy, in the module that already owns the account lifecycle.

The startup reconcile moves into `runReefChannelLifecycle`, and activation moves behind a new `onReady` hook so the original ordering is preserved exactly — refresh peer keys, activate, then start the inbox — since an agent turn must not use Reef outbound before peer keys are refreshed. Both call sites now route through one internal `runReconcileStep` helper.

Deliberate boundary: on a startup failure the account continues with the peer keys already persisted, which is the same staleness the periodic path already tolerates between intervals, and the next interval retries. Two adjacent fixes fall out of the restructure — the abort listener on `parentSignal` is no longer leaked if a startup step throws, and an already-aborted account no longer issues a relay request on its way out.

## User Impact

Reef survives relay rate limiting instead of dying to it. When the relay throttles at startup, the account now comes up, logs `reef friend reconcile failed: ...`, serves inbound and outbound messages with the peer keys it already has, and refreshes them on the next 30s reconcile once the relay recovers. Operators no longer need to restart the process to get Reef back, and Reef stops adding restart traffic to a relay that is already throttling.

No configuration change. The only behavior difference on the success path is that peer keys may briefly be one interval stale after a failed startup refresh.

## Evidence

Live run against a local relay returning `429 {"error":"rate_limited"}` on `GET /v1/friends`, driving the real `ReefTransportClient` — real request signing, real `ReefRelayError` — through both startup sequences:

```
local relay on http://127.0.0.1:59686 (429 on every request)

main (bare `await reconcile()` at channel.ts:405):
  [relay] GET /v1/friends -> 429
  startAccount: THREW -> ReefRelayError: rate_limited
  activated=false inboxStarted=false

patched (startup reconcile inside runReefChannelLifecycle):
  [relay] GET /v1/friends -> 429
  startAccount: still running (no throw)
  activated=true inboxStarted=true
  reported: ReefRelayError: rate_limited
  clean shutdown after abort
```

Harness scope: it drives the real transport, signing and lifecycle, and substitutes the trust-store bookkeeping that wraps `listFriends` inside `friends.reconcile()`. That bookkeeping is not what throws, and this machine cannot open the plugin state DB (see the note below).

**Tests** — two added to `extensions/reef/src/channel.test.ts`:

- `activates and starts the inbox when the startup reconcile fails` captures the reconcile and error counts *inside* `onReady`, so it pins the startup reconcile specifically rather than "some reconcile eventually failed" after the periodic loop has had a chance to run.
- `refreshes peer keys before activating and before the inbox starts` pins the `reconcile → ready → inbox` ordering.

Both are load-bearing — restoring a bare `await params.reconcile()` at startup fails them:

```
× activates and starts the inbox when the startup reconcile fails
× keeps running when a periodic reconcile fails
  Tests  3 failed | 5 passed (8)
```

`tears down the inbox loop before settling when a loop branch throws` needed one adjustment. It drives its failure through `onReconcileError` throwing, which now also fires on the startup step, so the inbox would never start and there would be nothing to tear down. Its startup reconcile now succeeds and the failure lands on the periodic loop with the inbox running, which is the case that test was written to cover.

**Local checks:** `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the three files, `tsgo --noEmit` clean, `extensions/reef/src/channel.test.ts` 7 passed / 1 failed.

That one failure is `exposes locally trusted peers as routable directory entries`, which fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` here (1 failed / 5 passed): this machine runs Node 22.20.0, whose embedded SQLite 3.50.4 is below the WAL-safety floor the plugin state store requires. Unrelated to this change. The `max-lines` ratchet likewise reports `ui/src/components/lobster-pet.ts` on this base with and without this change; not touched here.

target.title: fix(telegram-miniapp): cancel unread response body on auth error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Telegram Mini App page receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 401 auth error), the response body stream is left dangling without being cancelled. This can leak connections and waste resources in the Mini App's WebView environment.

**Root Cause**: The `renderTelegramMiniAppPage()` function's `fetch("auth", ...)` handler was missing `response.body?.cancel()` before `throw new Error("auth failed")`, leaving the response body stream unread and un-cancelled on auth errors.

**Solution**: Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw, matching the established codebase pattern used across `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and other extensions.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Local HTTP server simulating Telegram auth endpoint (401 response), Node.js `fetch` API.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Rendered Telegram Mini App page: extract inline script & verify body cancel on auth failure
node docs/.local/issue-109983/verify-rendered.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence** (`docs/.local/issue-109983/verify.log`):
```
=== Step 1: Rendered HTML verification ===
HTML length: 2255
Contains auth POST method: true
Contains body cancel: true
Contains .catch(() => undefined): true

=== Step 2: Rendered auth-fetch code (extracted) ===
fetch("auth", {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify({ initData, accountId }),
        credentials: "same-origin",
        signal: authController.signal
      }).then(async (response) => {
        if (!response.ok) {
          response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
          throw new Error("auth failed");
        }

=== Step 3: End-to-end body cancel via live HTTP ===
Response status: 401
Response ok: false
Body locked before cancel: false
Body locked after cancel: false
Cancel executed without unhandled rejection: YES
Body read after cancel returns done: true
```

target.title: fix(ci): sweep PRs with unknown mergeability in pr-ci-sweeper
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The hourly PR CI sweeper (#110889) never repaired its primary targets. Live verification found three genuinely dropped-CI PRs (#110837, #110776, #110657) skipped as `mergeability-pending` across three consecutive sweeps: their `mergeable` stays `null` / `mergeable_state: "unknown"` indefinitely, so the conservative guard made exactly the PRs the sweeper exists for permanently unsweepable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Probing showed the stuck merge-ref computation IS the pathology: repeated `pulls.get` calls over 16+ seconds never resolve mergeability for dropped-CI PRs, while healthy PRs compute within seconds. Close/reopen is what un-sticks GitHub's merge-ref machinery (validated on four maintainer PRs this week). The classify guard now re-fires on unknown mergeability and keeps skipping computed conflicts (`mergeable: false`); the pre-close revalidation applies the same policy. A not-yet-computed conflict costs at most one budgeted re-fire before the post-reopen recomputation yields `false` and skips it — bounded by the existing per-PR budget of two closes.

## User Impact

The sweeper actually heals dropped PR CI instead of logging skips forever. No other behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Live sweep logs (runs 29657783396, 29659015960): `skip #110837/#110776/#110657 (mergeability-pending)` with zero re-fires despite those heads having zero pull_request CI runs.
- Direct probes: `mergeable: null`, `mergeable_state: "unknown"` persisting across repeated GETs 16+ seconds apart for #110837.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/pr-ci-sweeper.test.ts` — 14 tests pass with the inverted null-mergeability case.
- Structured autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol): clean (0.97).
- Post-merge: live dispatch must show re-fires on the three stuck PRs and CI attaching to their heads.

target.title: fix(canvas): restore shipped policy/host-disable contracts; harden workspaces doctor cleanup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reviewer follow-ups from the canvas-core promotion (#110475) and workspaces removal (#110416): two shipped-config compatibility gaps and two doctor-safety gaps, flagged as P1/P2 by review bots on those PRs. Also lands the session-dashboard architecture doc.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `tools.deny: ["canvas"]` silently stopped covering `show_widget` after it moved to core — the canvas policy family now includes it again (shipped operator-config contract).
- The shipped canvas host disable switches (`plugins.entries.canvas.config.host.enabled=false`, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CANVAS_HOST`) now disable core widget serving, capability advertisement, and tool registration, as they did pre-promotion.
- `doctor --fix` retired-workspaces cleanup now requires plugin-state fingerprints and skips (with a warning) any directory that overlaps a configured agent workspace — including nested, ancestor, and symlinked paths — so it can never delete user data on a path collision.
- Report-only `openclaw doctor` now surfaces the stale-workspaces warning instead of only acting under `--fix`.
- Adds `docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md` (the design doc this program builds from) to the docs nav.

## User Impact

Restores two shipped operator contracts broken by the core promotion; makes the new doctor cleanup provably safe; no new config surface.

## Evidence

Focused suites green: doctor 101/101, policy 36/36, gateway 7/7. `check-changed` fully green on Testbox. Autoreview clean. Allow/deny and disable-switch paths covered by new tests; workspace-collision cases (nested/ancestor/symlink) tested.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 400: body cancelled 66ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 403: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 500: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 429: body cancelled 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 503: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Null body: safe (no error on missing body) 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Cancel rejection: suppressed 1ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
All non-2xx paths call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing, verified across status codes 400, 403, 429, 500, 503. Null body and cancellation rejection edge cases are also handled.

**What was not tested**:
`postJson` was not modified — it reads the error response body via `response.json()` to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### Fix 2: Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > demonstrates the JSON.parse try-catch improvement 96ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > gracefully handles malformed ADC file via config resolver 3ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
Malformed JSON at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` now produces `Error("Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: /path/to/file")` instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. The `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` caller catches this and returns `undefined`, so `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` degrades gracefully instead of crashing.

**What was not tested**:
The fix is in `readGoogleAdcCredentials` which is called from two paths: (a) `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` used by `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync`, and (b) `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders`. Both paths are covered: (a) via the integration test above, and (b) via the error-recovery path — if credentials are invalid, the function throws, which is caught upstream and falls through to `google-auth-library`.

## Tests and validation

### Evidence tests

Both evidence test suites pass at exact HEAD `cab77b1ef899c5734eb4a686873ed880f075cd14`:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
- merge-risk: auth-provider — both fixes add defensive guards without changing auth flow or error semantics. The Vertex ADC fix wraps an existing error path in a clearer message; the QA Lab fix adds body cleanup before existing throws. No credential path, token exchange, or provider selection logic is altered.

target.title: fix(markdown): keep IR text slicing UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added surrogate pair boundary detection to `sliceMarkdownIR` in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`. Before slicing text, start/end indices are now checked and adjusted to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. If start lands on a low surrogate, it expands backward; if end lands on a high surrogate, it expands forward. The same adjusted boundaries are applied consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. Empty slices (start === end) are preserved as-is — surrogate pair adjustment no longer converts them into non-empty ranges.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the public API of `sliceMarkdownIR`, no changes to any other files, no behavioral changes for text that does not contain surrogate pairs (ASCII/ISO-8859 text is unaffected). Empty-slice callers continue to receive empty text.

Fixes #110643

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When slicing markdown IR text, the raw `start`/`end` indices may land in the middle of a UTF-16 surrogate pair, producing invalid text with a dangling high or low surrogate character. Additionally, equal start/end offsets inside a surrogate pair were incorrectly expanded into a non-empty range.

**Behavior addressed**: Ensure `sliceMarkdownIR` adjusts slice boundaries to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs, producing valid text output, while preserving empty slices (insertion points) as empty.

**Root Cause**: In `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`, `sliceMarkdownIR` passes indices directly to `String.prototype.slice()` without checking surrogate pair boundaries. Characters outside the BMP (e.g. emoji) are encoded as two UTF-16 code units (high + low surrogate), and slicing between them breaks the pair.

**Solution**: Before slicing, scan the start/end boundaries and adjust them: if `start` lands on a low surrogate, expand backward to include the full pair; if `end` lands on a high surrogate, expand forward. Apply the same adjusted boundaries consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. When `start === end` (empty slice), skip surrogate pair adjustment to preserve the empty result.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**: All 9 surrogate pair boundary tests pass — covering start-on-low-surrogate, split-between-pair, clean-boundaries, start-on-high-surrogate, multiple-consecutive-pairs, negative-start-index, adjusted-boundaries-to-link-spans, plus 2 new tests for equal start/end offsets inside surrogate pairs (both on LS and HS).

**Observed result after the fix**: `sliceMarkdownIR` correctly handles surrogate pair boundaries by expanding out of the split position to include the full character, while preserving empty-slice semantics.

**What was not tested**: N/A — the fix is fully covered by the 9 unit tests.

## Tests and validation

<details>
<summary>Test output (9/9 passed)</summary>

```
$ pnpm test packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts

 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > expands start boundary backward when it lands on a low surrogate
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > expands end boundary forward when it splits between HS and LS
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves full text when boundaries are already clean
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > leaves boundaries unchanged when start is on a high surrogate
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > handles multiple consecutive surrogate pairs
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > handles negative start index
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > propagates adjusted boundaries to link spans
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves empty slice when start === end lands inside a surrogate pair
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves empty slice when start === end lands on a high surrogate

      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

[AI-assisted]
## What Problem This Solves

Wear OS users currently have to move through separate Agent and Session pages to change conversation context, while the active model cannot be selected from Home. That makes frequent context changes slow and consumes limited space on a round Watch display.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves agent, session, and model selection into three compact previous/next controls on Home, removes the redundant Agent and Session pages, and reduces the main pager to Home/Chat, Voice, and Controls. Model discovery and selection use a capability-negotiated Phone proxy contract and remain bound to the selected session.

## User Impact

Wear OS users can switch agent, session, and model without leaving Home, with fewer pages to swipe through. Existing chat, voice, and control workflows remain available, and unsupported model controls stay disabled with older Phone builds.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body in parity tool-call fetch
target.body:
## Summary

`loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` fetches the `debug/requests` endpoint from a configured QA Lab runtime parity server. When the endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status (503, 400, 500), the function returns null early without consuming the response body stream, leaving an unread stream resource dangling that may hold the connection open.

The fix adds `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the early return on `!response.ok`. This cancels the unread body stream, matching the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path.

**What changed**: One line added in `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` at `runtime-parity.ts:1055`. No changes to the ok path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the ok response path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality. No new dependencies or configuration options added.

Fixes #109991

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` returns null early on non-ok HTTP responses without cancelling the unread response body stream, potentially leaking resources and holding connections open.

**Root Cause**: At `runtime-parity.ts:1055`, the `!response.ok` early-return path calls `return null` without first cancelling the response body stream via `response.body?.cancel()`. The ok path implicitly drains the body via `response.json()`, but the non-ok path has no such cleanup.

**Solution**: Add `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before returning null on non-ok responses. This mirrors the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path. The `.catch(() => undefined)` guard ensures safety even if the body stream is already in an inconsistent state.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Body cancel on non-ok HTTP response in QA Lab runtime parity mock tool-call fetch path.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic / Node.js 22 / OpenClaw 2026.7.2 / HTTP mock server (127.0.0.1) exercising `captureRuntimeParityCell` with non-ok debug/requests endpoint responses.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# 1. Direct HTTP interaction showing body cancel on non-ok response
node --input-type=module -e "
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
const server = createServer((req, res) => {
  res.statusCode = 503;
  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Service Unavailable' }));
});
await new Promise(r => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', r));
const addr = server.address();
const port = addr.port;
console.log('Mock server on port ' + port);
const resp = await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:' + port + '/debug/requests');
console.log('GET /debug/requests -> ' + resp.status + ' ' + resp.statusText);
console.log('Response ok: ' + resp.ok);
await resp.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
console.log('body.cancel() OK');
server.close();
"

# 2. Full evidence test suite
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity-body-cancel.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
# Direct HTTP interaction:
Mock server started on port 43353
GET /debug/requests -> 503 Service Unavailable
Response ok: false
body.cancel() OK -- no unread stream leak

# Evidence test suite:

 ✓ handles 400 Bad Request without crashing
 ✓ handles 500 Internal Server Error without crashing

      Tests  4 passed (4)

# Existing parity test suite (no regression):

      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The HTTP mock server returns 503 and the body is cancelled cleanly. All 4 evidence tests pass — body cancel fires before returning null on 503/400/500, and null mockBaseUrl is handled without attempting a fetch. The existing 16 parity tests also pass with no regression.

**What was not tested**: Full integration against a live deployed QA Lab runtime gateway. The HTTP mock server exercises the exact code path (real `captureRuntimeParityCell`, real fetch Response objects) but is not a pre-configured QA Lab deployment. The body cancel behavior is identical regardless of which endpoint serves the response.

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

target.title: feat(clients): adopt model controls, session management, and keyboard history recall on iOS
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS/web chat parity rounds (#110254, #110276, #110339, #110347) landed all capability in shared `OpenClawKit`, but iOS still only forwarded transport fields: no model controls, no session groups/batch/inspector, no worktree-aware creation, and no hardware-keyboard input history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adopt the shared surfaces on iOS with iOS-idiomatic UX, keeping the shared API additive:

- **Model controls** (`ChatModelControlsMenu.swift`, wired from ChatPro's existing action menu): provider-grouped model picker via the shared `ChatModelPickerStore` (pinned + recents first, default badges), thinking with `Default (inherited)`, Fast as Default/On/Off (Default patches `fastMode: null`; display rides `effectiveFastMode`; legacy `auto` not re-selectable), verbosity as Default/off/on/full (Default patches null).
- **Session management**: the sessions affordance now presents the shared `ChatSessionsSheet` (groups, select/batch mode, inspector); advanced new-session options (agent, managed worktree, base ref) present in a medium-detent sheet.
- **Transport** (`IOSGatewayChatTransport.swift`): exact-route leases for settings, mutations, groups, and new-session; 6-arg `createSession` mapping `agentId`/`worktree`/`worktreeBaseRef`; settings patches forward the fast-mode double-optional including explicit null. Implementing the real overload removes iOS from the fail-closed protocol default.
- **Input history**: hardware-keyboard ↑ starts recall only from an empty draft; active recall supports ↑/↓; non-empty and soft-wrapped drafts keep native caret movement; no touch-UX change (shared `ChatInputHistory` state machine).

## User Impact

iOS chat users get the same model, Fast, verbosity, and thinking controls as web/macOS, full session organization (groups, batch actions, inspector, worktree sessions from a chosen base ref), and terminal-style input history on hardware keyboards.

## Evidence

- Shared OpenClawKit suite: 994 tests green (48 XCTest + 946 Swift Testing, 81+ suites).
- iOS `build-for-testing` (generic simulator, Xcode project via xcodegen): green — app and test targets compile.
- `IOSGatewayChatTransportTests`: 15/15, including advanced-create encoding, fast-mode set/null, and groups-lease methods/params/decoding.
- `pnpm format:swift` clean; `pnpm lint:swift` 0 violations; all touched files under the 1500-line cap; `git diff --check` clean.
- i18n: new strings translated across all locales; `pnpm native:i18n:check` clean; apple/android i18n vitest gates green.
- Autoreview (branch mode): "patch is correct", zero accepted/actionable findings (one earlier P2 — soft-wrapped draft caret interception — found and fixed during development).
- Known non-gate: the local-only `OpenClawTypographyTests` broad source audit flags pre-existing lines in untouched shared/macOS files; CI's `ios-build` job compiles but does not execute the iOS test bundle, and the new controls use branded typography.

target.title: fix(agents): repeated tool-call ids bind results to the wrong call on replay
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Related: #110518

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where replaying a session across models could feed the model a fabricated tool result while silently discarding a real one.

`transformTransportMessages` rewrites tool-call ids for cross-model replay and keys the rewrites in a flat `Map<rawId, newId>`. Providers do reuse the same tool-call id across turns — that is the premise of #110518 — and with last-write-wins every result pointed at the most recent rewrite.

For a transcript with two assistant turns that both used provider id `call_1`, followed by their two results, the first call ends up with no result of its own. Shared repair then synthesizes a placeholder for it, the first real output is attached to the second call, and the second real output is dropped entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

#110518 fixed exactly this ordering hazard in the two sibling pipelines, and states the reason in the code it added: *"Pair raw provider-id occurrences before rewriting ids. On a damaged transcript, FIFO id rewriting can otherwise bind a later-adjacent result to an older call."*

- `embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts` — pairing moved ahead of the id rewrite, `sanitizeToolCallIds` forced to `false` in the earlier stage.
- `embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.tool-call-normalization.ts` — pairing moved ahead of `sanitizeToolCallIdsForCloudCodeAssist`.

`transport-message-transform.ts` is the third pipeline that performs both operations, and the same commit touched it — adding `failedAssistantHasToolCalls` so that shared repair could see errored tool-call frames alongside their results, with a comment noting that pre-filtering "can misattribute its result to an older turn that reused the same provider id". The id-rewrite map itself was left keyed by raw id.

Rather than reorder this pipeline (its rewrite is interleaved with thinking-block handling in a single pass), the map now queues the rewrites per raw id and each result consumes one in order. When a call carries more results than it has occurrences, the most recent rewrite is reused, preserving today's behavior for that case.

## User Impact

Sessions replayed onto a different model no longer show a tool result the model never produced, and no longer lose a real tool result, when the source provider reused a tool-call id across turns. Transcripts with unique ids are unaffected.

## Evidence

Before/after on the same transcript, driving the public `transformTransportMessages` export. `origin/main` was materialized side by side with this branch's HEAD:

```
Transcript: two assistant turns both using provider id call_1, then OUTPUT-A and OUTPUT-B.

main:
  assistant toolCall  id=n1_call_1
  toolResult  id=n1_call_1  content=[{"type":"text","text":"No result provided"}]
  assistant toolCall  id=n2_call_1
  toolResult  id=n2_call_1  content=OUTPUT-A

HEAD:
  assistant toolCall  id=n1_call_1
  toolResult  id=n1_call_1  content=OUTPUT-A
  assistant toolCall  id=n2_call_1
  toolResult  id=n2_call_1  content=OUTPUT-B
```

On `main` the first call receives a synthesized `No result provided`, `OUTPUT-A` is misattributed to the second call, and `OUTPUT-B` disappears. On this branch each result pairs with the call it belongs to.

<details>
<summary>Proof harness</summary>

```ts
import { transformTransportMessages as head } from "./src/agents/transport-message-transform.js";
import { transformTransportMessages as main } from "./src/agents/transport-message-transform.mainproof.js";

const model = {
  api: "anthropic-messages", provider: "anthropic", id: "claude-opus-4-6",
  name: "claude-opus-4-6", input: [], output: [],
} as never;

function transcript() {
  const ts = 1;
  return [
    { role: "assistant", provider: "openai", api: "openai-responses", model: "gpt-5.4",
      stopReason: "toolUse", timestamp: ts,
      content: [{ type: "toolCall", id: "call_1", name: "read", arguments: {} }] },
    { role: "assistant", provider: "openai", api: "openai-responses", model: "gpt-5.4",
      stopReason: "toolUse", timestamp: ts,
      content: [{ type: "toolCall", id: "call_1", name: "read", arguments: {} }] },
    { role: "toolResult", toolCallId: "call_1", toolName: "read", content: "OUTPUT-A", timestamp: ts },
    { role: "toolResult", toolCallId: "call_1", toolName: "read", content: "OUTPUT-B", timestamp: ts },
  ] as never;
}

function run(label: string, fn: typeof head): void {
  let n = 0;
  const out = fn(transcript(), model, (id: string) => `n${++n}_${id}`);
  console.log(`\n${label}:`);
  for (const m of out) {
    if (m.role === "assistant") {
      for (const b of (Array.isArray(m.content) ? m.content : [])) {
        if (b.type === "toolCall") console.log(`  assistant toolCall  id=${b.id}`);
      }
    } else if (m.role === "toolResult") {
      const c = typeof m.content === "string" ? m.content : JSON.stringify(m.content);
      console.log(`  toolResult  id=${m.toolCallId}  content=${c}`);
    }
  }
}

run("main", main as typeof head);
run("HEAD", head);
```

The `.mainproof.ts` copy was produced with `git show origin/main:src/agents/transport-message-transform.ts` and removed afterwards.

</details>

### Regression coverage

Two tests added to `transport-message-transform.test.ts`:

- Two calls sharing a provider id followed by two results pair in order (`n1`→first, `n2`→second). This test fails on `origin/main`; verified by stashing only the source change, which leaves the other 30 tests passing.
- A result displaced past an intervening user turn still pairs with the call it follows — this passes both before and after, guarding the reordering behavior against regression.

Local checks: `transport-message-transform`, `session-transcript-repair` and `attempt.tool-call-normalization` suites pass (41 tests), `run-tsgo` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean.

target.title: fix(agents): agent-created files get lowercased names on Windows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, files and directories an agent creates get **lowercased names**. Ask for
`src/Components/MyComponent.tsx` and what lands on disk is `src\components\mycomponent.tsx`.

NTFS is case-insensitive but case-*preserving*, so nothing fails locally — the agent reads its own file
back fine. The damage shows up downstream: git records the lowercased name, and the TypeScript/React
import the agent just wrote (`./Components/MyComponent`) resolves on the author's Windows box but breaks
for every teammate on Linux/macOS and in CI. Any agent-authored name that is not already lowercase is
affected: `README.md`, `Dockerfile`, `MyClass.ts`.

For some names it is worse than a case change. `"İstanbul.md".toLowerCase()` is `"i̇stanbul.md"` —
U+0130 becomes the two code points U+0069 U+0307, one longer than the original and not reversible. So a
Turkish filename does not come back lowercased, it comes back **corrupted**.

This is Windows-only. The POSIX branch of the same function preserves case correctly today.

## Why This Change Was Made

`toRelativePathUnderRoot` (`src/agents/path-policy.ts:76-90`) ran both root and candidate through
`normalizeWindowsPathForComparison` and then **returned** the resulting relative path:

```ts
const rootForCompare = normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(rootResolved);
const targetForCompare = normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(resolvedCandidate);
const relative = path.win32.relative(rootForCompare, targetForCompare);
return validateRelativePathWithinBoundary({ relativePath: relative, ... });
```

That helper lowercases (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.1`, `dist/path.js:17` →
`normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(...)`). Lowercasing is right for a **comparison key** — which is exactly
how the other two call sites use it — but this function hands the relative path back to callers, and they
build files out of it:

- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:1089-1092` — `mkdir`: `path.resolve(root, relative)` → `fs.mkdir`
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:1059-1060` — `writeWorkspaceFile` → `.write(relative, { mkdir: true })`
- `src/agents/apply-patch.ts:310,318,326` — `apply_patch` writeFile / remove / mkdirp

`toCanonicalRelativeWorkspacePath` (`agent-tools.read.ts:1167-1179`) does not rescue it: `fs.realpath`
restores the true case only of the **already-existing** ancestor, the new basename stays lowercased, and
line 1179 re-lowercases the whole thing on the way out. `assertSandboxPath` does not either — it is
handed the already-derived `resolved` path, not the original candidate.

The lowercasing was also never needed for the boundary math. `path.win32.relative` already matches the
root case-insensitively **and** returns the tail in its original case, so the pre-lowercasing bought
nothing and cost the filename. The one part of that normalization the boundary check does rely on is
extended-length prefix stripping — without it a `\\?\C:\...` candidate relativizes to
`..\..\..\?\C:\...` and gets rejected as an escape. So this adds `normalizeWindowsPathPreservingCase`
next to the comparison variant in `src/infra/path-guards.ts`. It mirrors that helper step for step —
including the trim — minus the lowercasing, and a test pins that equivalence directly so the two cannot
drift:

```ts
expect(normalizeWindowsPathPreservingCase(input).toLowerCase()).toBe(
  normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(input),
);
```

### Sibling surfaces

All three callers of `normalizeWindowsPathForComparison` were checked. Only this one was misusing it:

| Call site | Uses result as | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts:215` | comparison key (`===`) | correct, untouched |
| `isPathInside` (fs-safe) | discards relative, returns boolean | correct, untouched |
| `src/agents/path-policy.ts` | **returns it to callers** | fixed here |

## Evidence

**Live before/after on real Windows** (Windows 11, NTFS, Turkish locale), driving the real
`toRelativeWorkspacePath` through the exact call pattern of `agent-tools.read.ts`, then reading the names
back with `fs.readdirSync`:

Before (`origin/main`):

```
--- case 1: agent asked for src\Components\MyComponent.tsx ---
  toRelativeWorkspacePath -> "src\components\mycomponent.tsx"
  ON DISK                 -> components/mycomponent.tsx

--- case 2: agent asked for İstanbul.md ---
  asked   : İstanbul.md  | length 11 | U+0130
  ON DISK : i̇stanbul.md | length 12 | U+0069 U+0307
  identical? NO  <- filename corrupted, not just lowercased
```

After (this branch):

```
--- case 1: agent asked for src\Components\MyComponent.tsx ---
  toRelativeWorkspacePath -> "src\Components\MyComponent.tsx"
  ON DISK                 -> Components/MyComponent.tsx

--- case 2: agent asked for İstanbul.md ---
  asked   : İstanbul.md | length 11 | U+0130
  ON DISK : İstanbul.md | length 11 | U+0130 U+0073
  identical? YES
```

**Why the existing test did not catch it:** `path-policy.test.ts:23` used an all-lowercase candidate
(`c:/users/user/openclaw/memory/log.txt`), which passes either way. The new cases use mixed case.

**Tests** — every added mixed-case assertion fails on `origin/main` and passes here:

```
path-policy.test.ts + path-guards.test.ts        41/41 passed
+ agent-tools.workspace-paths, apply-patch,
  installed-plugin-index-record-reader            111 passed | 12 skipped, 0 failed
max-lines ratchet                                 OK
dead-export ratchet (knip)                        0 entries
oxlint / oxfmt --check                            clean
tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json                        no errors in touched files
```

## Merge Risk

Low, but this touches a sandbox boundary, so here is the containment argument explicitly.

**The boundary decision is unchanged.** `path.win32.relative` compares case-insensitively, so
`relative(lower(a), lower(b))` and `relative(a, b)` return the same *structure* — same number of `..`
segments, same segment count, same absoluteness. Only the case of the returned characters differs.
`validateRelativePathWithinBoundary` looks at exactly that structure (`""`/`"."`, `".."`, `"../"`,
`"..\\"`, `isAbsolute`), so every accept/reject verdict is identical. Verified empirically:

```
root: C:\Users\User\OpenClaw
escape, no lowercasing        -> "..\Other\log.txt"     still rejected
root itself, differing case   -> ""                     allowRoot still honored
drive-letter case c: vs C:    -> "Memory\Log.txt"       still matched
\\?\ prefix NOT stripped      -> "..\..\..\?\C:\..."    why stripping is kept
```

Two of the added tests pin this directly — an escape that differs from the root only by case is still
rejected, and a differently-cased root still resolves to `""` under `allowRoot`. Both pass before and
after the change, which is the point.

Scope is one file's Windows branch plus one new helper with a single caller. POSIX behavior is untouched.

AI-assisted.
