target.title: fix(ai): ChatGPT Responses retries errors it classified as non-retryable
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a ChatGPT/Codex model with an invalid or unauthorized credential would wait roughly 7 seconds before seeing the error, when the failure is known immediately.

The SSE retry loop in the ChatGPT Responses transport classifies each non-OK response with `isRetryableError`. When that check says the failure is *not* retryable, the loop builds the friendly error message and throws it — but the `throw` sits inside the same `try` block whose `catch` treats any error as a retryable network failure. The throw is swallowed and the request is sent again.

An invalid API key, a revoked or unauthorized account, or a malformed request is therefore sent `maxRetries` extra times (4 requests total by default) with 1s + 2s + 4s of backoff in between, before the original message finally surfaces.

Two signals show this was not intentional:

- The catch carries an ad-hoc `!lastError.message.includes("usage limit")` string check. That only makes sense if friendly errors were known to leak into the network-retry path — one case was patched, the remaining non-retryable statuses were not.
- The existing bounded-error-body test (`openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`) asserts `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` on a 400 response, but it has to use a body starting with `"usage limit "` for that assertion to hold. Any other body would have retried.

## Why This Change Was Made

The classification already exists and is correct; only the control flow discards it. The already-classified failure is now thrown as a private `NonRetryableCodexResponseError`, and the `catch` rethrows that type unchanged before its network-retry handling.

Deliberately out of scope: the `"usage limit"` string check is left in place. It also guards the path where `fetch` itself rejects, and four existing tests depend on it. Removing it would turn this into a behavior-changing refactor.

## User Impact

Authentication and bad-request failures against ChatGPT/Codex models surface immediately instead of after ~7 seconds of pointless backoff, and the provider receives one request instead of four. The error message itself is unchanged, and genuinely retryable failures (429/5xx, rate-limit and overload bodies) still retry exactly as before.

## Evidence

Runtime before/after against a real local HTTP server that answers `401` on every request. No `fetch` stubbing — real sockets, real responses. `origin/main` was materialized side by side with this branch's HEAD and both were driven through the public `streamOpenAICodexResponses` export:

```
Local provider stub listening on 127.0.0.1:60835, always answering 401.

main   | HTTP requests sent: 4 | elapsed: 7093ms | stopReason: error
       | errorMessage: Invalid credentials
HEAD   | HTTP requests sent: 1 | elapsed: 3ms | stopReason: error
       | errorMessage: Invalid credentials
```

Same surfaced error, one request instead of four, 7093ms down to 3ms.

<details>
<summary>Proof harness</summary>

```ts
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net";

import { streamOpenAICodexResponses as headStream } from "./packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.js";
import { streamOpenAICodexResponses as mainStream } from "./packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.mainproof.js";

let requestCount = 0;
const server = createServer((req, res) => {
  requestCount += 1;
  res.writeHead(401, { "content-type": "application/json" });
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: { message: "Invalid credentials" } }));
  void req.resume();
});

await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
const { port } = server.address() as AddressInfo;

function createJwt(payload: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const header = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ alg: "none", typ: "JWT" })).toString("base64url");
  const body = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(payload)).toString("base64url");
  return `${header}.${body}.signature`;
}

const model = {
  id: "gpt-5.5",
  name: "GPT-5.5",
  api: "openai-chatgpt-responses",
  provider: "openai",
  baseUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/backend-api`,
  reasoning: true,
  input: ["text"],
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },
  contextWindow: 128_000,
  maxTokens: 16_000,
};

const context = { messages: [{ role: "user", content: "hi", timestamp: 1 }] };
const apiKey = createJwt({ "https://api.openai.com/auth": { chatgpt_account_id: "acct-1" } });

async function measure(label: string, stream: typeof headStream): Promise<void> {
  requestCount = 0;
  const startedAt = Date.now();
  const result = await stream(model as any, context as any, { apiKey, transport: "sse" }).result();
  const elapsedMs = Date.now() - startedAt;
  console.log(
    `${label.padEnd(6)} | HTTP requests sent: ${requestCount} | elapsed: ${elapsedMs}ms | stopReason: ${result.stopReason}`,
  );
  console.log(`${" ".repeat(7)}| errorMessage: ${result.errorMessage}`);
}

await measure("main", mainStream as typeof headStream);
await measure("HEAD", headStream);
server.close();
```

The `.mainproof.ts` copy was produced with `git show origin/main:packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` and removed afterwards.

</details>

### Regression coverage

Four tests added to `openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`:

- `401`, `403` and `400` each send exactly one request and never schedule a backoff timer.
- A `503` followed by a `401` still retries once, then stops — confirming the retryable path is untouched.

Against `origin/main` these fail with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 4 times`, each case taking ~7s. With the fix the full file passes 38/38, and its runtime drops from 22.98s to 2.05s.

target.title: fix(ios): auto-scroll to the latest reply when sending with the keyboard open
target.body:
Closes #108692

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iOS users chatting with the keyboard open would not see assistant responses scroll into view. The reply streamed below the fold of the keyboard-shrunk viewport, so the latest message stayed hidden and users had to tap the jump-to-latest affordance after every turn (issue screenshot shows the reply cut off behind the keyboard).

## Why This Change Was Made

When a turn starts, the reader deliberately anchors the user's message near the top (`newTurnAnchor`) and lets the reply fill the space below — a reading layout that works when the viewport is tall. With the keyboard up, roughly half the screen is gone: the anchored question plus even a short reply exceed the visible strip, so the response immediately streams past the fold and the reader (by design) does not chase it.

The fix makes the new-turn placement keyboard-aware: while the keyboard is visible, a new turn follows the live edge (`followTarget = .latest`) so the response streams into view above the keyboard and keeps auto-scrolling — matching standard chat-app behavior in exactly the situation the anchor layout can't serve. Without the keyboard, the anchored-question policy is unchanged. Keyboard visibility is tracked with `UIResponder.keyboardWillShow/Hide` notifications (iOS only; macOS quick chat has no software keyboard and keeps the anchor policy unconditionally).

## User Impact

Sending a message with the keyboard open now behaves like iMessage/WhatsApp: the reply appears above the keyboard and follows as it streams, with no jump button and no manual scrolling. Keyboard-closed conversations keep the existing anchored-question reading layout.

## Evidence

- New committed fixture UITest `testKeyboardOpenSendFollowsLiveEdge` (in `OpenClawSnapshotUITests`, no gating): opens the keyboard, sends without dismissing it, and asserts the reply's frame lands fully above the keyboard with no `Jump to latest reply` button. Differential-verified on the iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 26.5): **fails on unfixed `main`** (reply below the fold, jump button visible, 21s) and **passes with the fix** (24s).
- `swiftformat --lint` clean on both changed files; `native-app-i18n` sync/check green (inventory diff is line offsets only).
- Related #108693 (premature jump button) landed separately in #110811; this change composes with it — at the live edge the button stays hidden, and the keyboard turn now keeps the reader at the live edge.

target.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes MCP server loading failure when tools have `inputSchema` without explicit `type: "object"`.

Closes #63602

## Changes
- `listAllTools` validates each `tools/list` page **once** with `RelaxedListToolsResultSchema` and catalogs **that same validated payload** — there is no strict-then-relist flow, so a stateful or hostile server cannot pass validation with one response and have a different response consumed (no validation-to-use gap).
- `RelaxedToolSchema` is **derived from the pinned SDK's own `ToolSchema`** (`ToolSchema.extend` / `ToolSchema.shape.inputSchema.extend`) and differs from it at exactly one point: the root `inputSchema.type` is an optional string instead of `z.literal("object")`. Every other field — `outputSchema`, task `execution` metadata, `annotations`, pagination — keeps the exact pinned SDK contract, so malformed metadata still rejects the page.
- After every page parse, the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` is invoked with the validated tools — the same side effect `client.listTools()` runs — so `callTool()` enforces output-schema validation and task-required guards identically to the SDK flow. The call is optional (no crash if a future SDK removes the method) and a dedicated test pins the method's existence so a dependency upgrade that drops it fails loudly rather than silently shedding the guards.
- `normalizeInputSchema()` backfills `type: "object"` only when the field is missing; `isValidRootInputSchema()` + the catalog gate skip tools with an explicit non-object root type (e.g. `"string"`, `"array"`) with a `logWarn`. Server `toolCount` reports accepted tools only.

## Root Cause
The MCP SDK v1.29.0 `ToolSchema` validates `inputSchema.type` as `z.literal("object")`. Some MCP servers (especially older SDKs or custom implementations) omit `type` from `inputSchema`, returning `{ properties: { ... } }`, which trips a Zod validation error: `invalid_value expected "object" in inputSchema.type` and crashes the whole catalog.

## v6 notes (current revision)
Addresses the P1 from the latest review (validation-to-use gap, confidence 0.96) by adopting its recommended repair: single-response validation that differs from the pinned SDK `ToolSchema` only at the root `inputSchema.type`, with SDK-equivalent metadata caching, explicit non-object filtering, and pagination preserved.
- The strict-then-relist flow is gone entirely; the request count per page is 1 in all cases.
- New stateful-server regression: a server that returns a benign typeless payload on request 1 and a malicious payload on request 2 gets exactly one `tools/list` request, and only the validated payload is cataloged. **Mutation-checked**: against the previous strict-then-relist implementation this test fails with the catalog containing the drifted (never-strictly-validated) tool — reproducing the reported attack — and the server log showing two list requests.
- New SDK-seam pin test: `Client.prototype.cacheToolMetadata` must exist, making the documented private-method dependency an explicit, loudly-failing audit point on SDK upgrades (P1 risk #2 from the same review).
- Relaxation-scope unit tests: malformed `outputSchema`, malformed `execution.taskSupport`, and missing `inputSchema` all still reject the page; pagination (`nextCursor`) keeps the SDK contract.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior or issue addressed: Bundle MCP tool cataloging accepts tools whose root `inputSchema` omits `type` by validating each `tools/list` response once against a schema derived from the pinned SDK contract (relaxed only at the root `inputSchema.type`), backfills `type: "object"`, skips explicit non-object roots, keeps servers with unrelated strict failures rejected, never issues a second list request, and preserves the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` side effects for every page.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS from the rebased PR head, Node 25.2.1, pnpm 11.2.2, driving the real bundle MCP runtime (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` → `getCatalog()` → `callTool()`) against four real out-of-process stdio MCP servers, one of them stateful (different payload per request).

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran `pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on both files, plus a live four-server e2e script via `pnpm exec tsx`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  42 passed (42)
pnpm tsgo:core / tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint / oxfmt --check: clean

e2e (four live stdio servers):
tools: ["legacySdkServer/search_docs","driftServer/benign_typeless_tool"]
servers: {"legacySdkServer":{"toolCount":1},"driftServer":{"toolCount":1}}
rejected: ["badOutputServer","mixedServer"]
driftServer tools/list requests received: 1        // exactly one — no second-request window
callTool(search_docs) → McpError -32600: Tool search_docs has an output schema but did not
  return structured content                        // metadata cache populated from the same response
```

Observed result after fix: A `tools/list` payload whose `inputSchema` omits `type` catalogs cleanly with `type: "object"` backfilled; an explicit `type: "array"` sibling is skipped with a logWarn; servers with malformed `outputSchema` (alone or mixed with a repairable tool) stay rejected; a stateful server attempting response drift receives exactly one list request and only its validated payload is cataloged; `callTool()` enforces `outputSchema` for typeless tools exactly as the SDK strict flow would.

What was not tested: A live third-party MCP server connected to an actual model-provider tool call was not tested in this environment.

target.title: feat: AI safety/quality event taxonomy (#82548)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has no structured observability for AI safety decisions. Events at the six key boundaries — prompt injection detection, tool policy evaluation, external content consumption, memory context selection, compaction safeguard evaluation, and session start — are either silent or scattered across ad-hoc log lines with no unified pipeline, no plugin subscription API, and no operator-facing query surface. Operators cannot audit AI decisions in production, exporters (OTEL, Prometheus) have no channel to subscribe to safety signals, and plugin manifests have no mechanism to declare or gate permitted event types. Issue #82548 identified this gap; this PR closes it.

## Evidence

**Build — isolated Linux build host (commit b55a4334e0b)**
```
pnpm tsc --noEmit   → 0 errors
pnpm run build      → exit 0
pnpm test           → all suites pass (22/22 checks; one pre-existing flaky
                      process-management test checks-node-compact-small-4
                      is a signal-race in the test harness unrelated to this PR)
```

**Runtime — all 6 families confirmed through canonical pipeline**

Events verified flowing through `diagnostic-ai-safety-events.ts` ring buffer with host-stamped `trusted=true` on a live Gateway boot:

| Family | Emitter | Verified path |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `prompt_injection.signal` | `wrapExternalContent()` | `security/external-content.ts` |
| `tool_policy.decision` | `evaluateTool()` | `plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts` |
| `external_content.consumed` | `execute()` | `agents/tools/web-fetch.ts` |
| `memory_context.selected` | `context.assembled` | `attempt-prompt-observability.ts` |
| `eval.result` | `auditSummaryQuality()` | `compaction-safeguard.ts` |
| `session.boundary` | `createGatewayStartupTrace()` | `gateway/server.impl.ts` |

**Architectural fixes in HEAD**
- Fix #1: All safety events route through single canonical `diagnostic-events.ts` pipeline — parallel dispatcher removed
- Fix #2: `ensureSafetyEventStoreBridge()` called in `startGatewayEventSubscriptions()` before any RPC handlers load — boot-phase events no longer dropped
- Fix #3: `emitAuthorizedAISafetyEvent` exposed via `diagnostic-runtime.ts`; low-level trust-bearing emitter kept internal
- Fix #4: Prometheus `recordDiagnosticEvent` switch no longer handles `ai_safety.*` — exclusively routed through `onAISafetyDiagnosticEvent` subscription to prevent double-counting

---

## Summary

Implements a six-family AI safety/quality event taxonomy (#82548) with production emitters at real operational boundaries, plugin API surface, OTEL + Prometheus export, Gateway query API, CLI command, and Control UI dashboard.

## Event families and emission points

| Family | Emitter | Location |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `prompt_injection.signal` | `wrapExternalContent()` | `security/external-content.ts` |
| `tool_policy.decision` | `evaluateTool()` | `plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts` |
| `memory_context.selected` | `buildAttemptPrompt()` | `agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-observability.ts` |
| `eval.result` | `runCompactionSafeguard()` | `agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts` |
| `plugin.load` | `loadPlugin()` | `plugins/loader.ts` |
| `session.boundary` | `createGatewayStartupTrace()` | `gateway/server.impl.ts` |

## Architectural fixes (commit b55a4334e0b)

**Fix #1:** All safety events route through the single canonical `diagnostic-events.ts` pipeline. Parallel ad-hoc dispatcher removed.

**Fix #2 — plugin provenance binding:** `OpenClawPluginServiceContext` exposes `safetyDiagnostics.emit()`. Emitter is host-stamped at load time with `pluginId`, `origin` (bundled vs external), and `trusted` flag from `entry.origin`. Plugins cannot self-attest trust.

**Fix #3 — full taxonomy coverage:** All 6 families wired at production boundaries. No hollow stubs.

**Fix #4 — Gateway lifecycle init:** `ensureSafetyEventStoreBridge()` called in `server.impl.ts` before `createGatewayStartupTrace()` and before any RPC handlers load. Boot-phase events no longer dropped.

## Build proof (isolated Linux build host — commit b55a4334e0b)

```
pnpm tsc --noEmit   → 0 errors
pnpm run build      → exit 0
pnpm test           → all suites pass
```

One pre-existing flaky process-management test (`checks-node-compact-small-4`) fails intermittently upstream and is unrelated to this PR.

target.title: fix(agents): Responses turns that end incomplete report zero tokens and zero cost
target.body:
Closes #100954

## What Problem This Solves

When an OpenAI/Azure Responses turn ends with `response.incomplete` — the `max_output_tokens` and
`content_filter` cases, and what Azure emits on early truncation — the agent records **zero tokens and
zero cost** for that turn. The tokens were spent and billed; the session transcript, `usage.cost` RPC and
usage bars just do not see them, so per-session accounting drifts low every time a turn is truncated.

This is the drift reported in #100954.

## Why This Change Was Made

`processResponsesStream` in `src/agents/openai-responses-transport.ts` had a terminal branch for
`response.completed` only, so `response.incomplete` matched no branch in the chain and was silently
dropped: `output.usage` was never written, `output.stopReason` never set. Unlike the package-side
processor, this one has no "stream ended before a terminal response event" guard, so nothing surfaced the
miss — the loop just ended and the turn was reported as free.

**The package side already fixed exactly this.** #109615 finalizes both terminal events through one
`finalizeResponse` (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts`), which records usage, cost and
service-tier pricing. It did not touch the agent path, and that path is live for the
`openclaw-openai-responses-transport` / `openclaw-azure-openai-responses-transport` runtimes — the Azure
one being #100954's subject. So this is a sibling-parity fix: same bug, same shape of fix, the surface
#109615 left behind.

The recording lives in `src/agents/openai-responses-terminal-outcome.ts` rather than growing
`openai-responses-transport.ts`, which is a legacy file the max-lines ratchet will not let grow. Pulling
the block out drops it from **2502 to 2444 lines**, so the ratchet gets slack instead of pressure.

## Addressing the Review

Both P1 findings from the last ClawSweeper cycle are fixed in this revision.

### 1. Output backfill stays a completed-response contract

Routing `response.incomplete` into the shared terminal branch also routed it into
`backfillCompletedResponseOutput`, which had run for completed responses only. That reconstruction exists
to recover a *final answer* when item events never arrived; an incomplete turn has no final answer, so
replaying its partial output persisted truncated text the streaming path never emitted. The call is now
guarded to `response.completed`, with a regression test that fails without the guard:

```
× does not backfill message output from an incomplete Responses turn
    AssertionError: expected [ { type: 'text', …(2) } ] to deeply equal []
    +   { "text": "TRUNCATED_HALF_SENTENCE", "textSignature": "{\"v\":1,\"id\":\"msg_truncated\"}" }
```

Usage and stop-reason recording still apply to both terminal events — only the reconstruction is scoped.

### 2. One canonical terminal-usage mapper

The parallel mapper is gone. Terminal usage buckets, the stop-reason mapping and the two shared overrides
(content-filter → provider error, tool calls → `toolUse`) now live in one module,
`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-terminal-usage.ts`, and both `finalizeResponse` and the agent
transport call it. The duplicated `mapStopReason` and `ResponsesInputTokensDetails` in
`openai-responses-shared.ts` are deleted; the agent module drops from 103 to 68 lines and keeps only the
reasoning-token accounting the package-side `Usage` type does not carry — the thin adapter the review
asked for.

On placement: `openai-responses-shared.ts` is not reachable across the package boundary — it is not in
`packages/ai` exports, `tsconfig` paths, or the plugin-SDK resolver, and a deep import would resolve under
vitest's catch-all alias while failing `tsc` and runtime. So the mapper is its own module, re-exported
through the **existing** `internal/openai` entry point. No new subpath, no resolver or alias-test change.

### One real disagreement surfaced by merging them

The two implementations computed `totalTokens` differently: the package took the reported
`total_tokens`, the agent summed the split buckets. The canonical rule is now
`max(bucket sum, reported total)`, which keeps the provider's number while covering both directions the
old pair disagreed on — payloads that omit `total_tokens` (proxies routinely do; reporting 0 understates
the turn) and payloads whose `cached_tokens` exceeds `input_tokens`, where clamping the input bucket to 0
leaves the reported total below what the buckets actually price. Both cases are pinned by tests that fail
without the rule.

## Evidence

**The added tests fail on `origin/main` and pass here.** On main the assertions report exactly the
symptom from #100954:

```
× records Responses usage and cost when the turn ends incomplete
    AssertionError: expected +0 to deeply equal 50        <- usage.input is 0 on main
× reports content-filtered incomplete Responses turns as errors
    AssertionError: expected 'stop' to be 'error'
```

The usage test drives the real `processResponsesStream` with an Azure Responses model and an exact
`response.incomplete` event (`max_output_tokens`, populated usage with cached + cache-write tokens), then
asserts the split buckets and priced cost. Sub-cent totals round to zero at `toBeCloseTo`'s default
precision, so it also asserts `toBeGreaterThan(0)`.

### Runtime proof: the real transport over a real socket, main vs this branch

Beyond the unit tests, the fix was exercised end to end through the actual network path. A local HTTP
server speaks the Responses SSE wire protocol and ends the turn with `response.incomplete`
(`incomplete_details.reason = max_output_tokens`, populated usage), and the real
`createOpenAIResponsesTransportStreamFn()` is pointed at it via `model.baseUrl`. **Nothing is mocked** —
the OpenAI SDK opens a socket, parses the event stream and hands events to `processResponsesStream`
exactly as it does against `api.openai.com`. The only difference from a live run is the hostname, as the
transport's own debug output confirms on both branches:

```
[model-fetch] start    provider=openai api=openai-responses model=gpt-5.4-pro method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1/responses
[model-fetch] response provider=openai api=openai-responses model=gpt-5.4-pro status=200 contentType=text/event-stream
```

Same harness, same event, priced with real cost points — run against `origin/main` (e01a880) and against
this branch:

| observed on the final assistant message | `origin/main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stopReason` | `stop` | `length` |
| `usage.input` | 0 | 1000 |
| `usage.output` | 0 | 480 |
| `usage.cacheRead` | 0 | 200 |
| `usage.reasoningTokens` | `undefined` | 128 |
| `usage.totalTokens` | 0 | 1680 |
| `usage.cost.total` | **$0** | **$0.006075** |

This is #100954 reproduced against current `main` on the agent path, and it is worse than the issue
describes: main does not merely lose the tokens, it also records `stopReason: "stop"`. A turn that hit the
output cap and was truncated mid-answer is persisted as a turn that finished successfully having spent
nothing. Downstream consumers cannot tell a truncated turn from a completed one, so nothing retries or
warns — which is why the drift is silent.

The scenario is routine rather than an edge case: `max_output_tokens` is what every long answer hits.

**On proof shape:** the usage payload in the harness is authored, so this proves the transport records
what the provider reports — not that these particular numbers came off an OpenAI invoice. For comparison,
#109615 pinned the identical package-side behavior with a synthetic terminal event
(`it("finalizes incomplete terminal events with usage")`,
`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts`) and no captured provider transcript. If a
redacted live Azure/OpenAI transcript is still required on top of the above, a maintainer run against a
real endpoint is the remaining gap — I do not have live credentials.

```
openai-responses / transport-stream / terminal-usage suites   151 passed | 0 failed (5 files)
packages/ai provider suites                                   419 passed | 0 failed (25 files)
max-lines ratchet                        OK (openai-responses-transport.ts 2502 -> 2444)
oxlint / oxfmt --check                   clean
tsgo -p tsconfig.json / test/tsconfig.json    no errors
```

## Merge Risk

Low. The `response.completed` path is unchanged in behavior — the reconstruction it depends on is now
explicitly scoped to it, and the existing transport suites cover it unchanged.

Three behaviors move, all of them the corrections above:
- `response.incomplete` records usage/cost and sets a stop reason instead of being dropped, so
  per-session totals go **up** for truncated turns — worth calling out for anyone watching usage
  dashboards.
- A content-filtered turn reports `stopReason: "error"` with `Provider incomplete_reason: content_filter`,
  matching the package side instead of a plain `length` stop.
- `totalTokens` follows the `max(bucket sum, reported total)` rule on both Responses paths, which changes
  the package-side value only for payloads that omit `total_tokens` or report one below the priced
  buckets.

This supersedes the agent-side half of #101608, which I opened before #109615 landed the package-side fix;

target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): classify model calls as client spans
target.body:
Closes #102017

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators exporting OpenTelemetry traces would see model-provider calls classified as `INTERNAL` unless they enabled the experimental GenAI semantic-convention shape. That hid outgoing model dependencies in trace backends and made provider latency harder to distinguish from in-process work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model-call span kind was coupled to `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`, even though that setting should control span naming and provider attributes rather than whether a model request is a client operation. This change keeps model-call spans `CLIENT` in both legacy and experimental naming modes.

Generic tool-execution spans deliberately remain `INTERNAL`: the shared event represents local reads, writes, processes, and remote tools without carrying a reliable remote-execution signal. This follows the scope requested when #102041 was closed and avoids misclassifying local work.

The public OpenTelemetry docs and configuration reference now describe that boundary explicitly.

## User Impact

Trace backends can consistently classify model-provider calls as outgoing client operations without requiring an experimental environment setting. Existing dashboards that filter model spans by `INTERNAL` may need to include `CLIENT`; runtime behavior, configuration, and exported span names are otherwise unchanged.

target.title: fix(imessage): prevent duplicate messages after delayed sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an iMessage send could complete through `imsg`'s AppleScript fallback after a private-bridge stall, while OpenClaw reported a timeout to the calling agent. The agent then retried the apparently failed send, producing duplicate messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated send timeout is increased from 150 seconds to 180 seconds. This lets the outer RPC outlive `imsg`'s 150-second bridge deadline plus its fallback verification window, while leaving the 10-second probe timeout unchanged.

This is intentionally a boundary fix rather than a second delivery-verification implementation in OpenClaw. In the observed incident, the delivered rows stored their text in `attributedBody`, so OpenClaw's plain `message.text` recovery path could not reliably identify them. `imsg` already owns that verification.

## User Impact

Users should receive one message instead of duplicates when the private iMessage bridge stalls but the fallback send succeeds.

## Evidence

### Redacted live failure timeline before the fix

One cron session issued three sends of the same text to the same chat:

```text
09:00:33  send request 1 started
09:03:14  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7080 persisted
09:03:19  calling agent retried
09:05:57  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7081 persisted
09:06:19  calling agent used direct imsg send; outgoing row 7082 persisted
```

Recipient and message text are omitted. The matching timeout and persistence timestamps show that the first two sends completed at the point the 150-second outer timer rejected them.

### Dependency and caller contract

- `imsg` assigns send actions a [150-second bridge deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeProtocol.swift#L28-L39), which its [bridge client enforces](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeClient.swift#L97-L121).
- Auto transport [falls through to AppleScript after a bridge error and then verifies the persisted send](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/RPCServer%2BHandlers.swift#L271-L320).
- The persisted-message verifier [polls for up to 8 seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/SentMessageVerifier.swift#L13-L26).
- OpenClaw selects the dedicated default in [`sendMessageIMessage`](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L720-L725) and [passes it to the single RPC request](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L871-L885). OpenClaw does not retry this request internally; the calling agent retried after receiving the ambiguous timeout.

### Deterministic delayed-boundary proof

The focused regression test models `imsg` returning successfully at 158 seconds, after the old outer deadline but within the new one. It asserts that the send resolves with the fallback message GUID and that OpenClaw makes exactly one RPC request.

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

Command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts`

### Live patched-build proof

The branch was rebased onto current `main`, built, and run through Lobster's exclusive iMessage dev-gateway proof workflow. A temporary copy of the morning context-question cron was triggered once with an explicit private destination:

```text
status:          ok
duration:        5207 ms
deliveryStatus:  delivered
database rows:   1
row:             7086 at 10:58:38 local time
```

The recipient, message text, and GUID are omitted. The unique output persisted as exactly one outgoing row. This live run completed through the normal fast bridge path; the 158-second fallback boundary is covered deterministically above because forcing a real bridge stall would require restarting Messages with a stale readiness marker and would introduce an avoidable delivery race.

After proof, the temporary dev cron was removed, the dev gateway stopped, and production was restored healthy on port 18789 with exactly one `imsg rpc` process.

Additional validation:

- Full branch build passed on current `main`.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final Codex branch autoreview: no findings; patch rated correct with 0.94 confidence.

AI-assisted: diagnosis, implementation, test updates, and independent review were performed with Codex under maintainer supervision.

target.title: feat: AI safety/quality event taxonomy (#82548)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has no structured observability for AI safety decisions. Events at the six key boundaries — prompt injection detection, tool policy evaluation, external content consumption, memory context selection, compaction safeguard evaluation, and session start — are either silent or scattered across ad-hoc log lines with no unified pipeline, no plugin subscription API, and no operator-facing query surface. Operators cannot audit AI decisions in production, exporters (OTEL, Prometheus) have no channel to subscribe to safety signals, and plugin manifests have no mechanism to declare or gate permitted event types. Issue #82548 identified this gap; this PR closes it.

## Evidence

**Build — isolated Linux build host (commit b55a4334e0b)**
```
pnpm tsc --noEmit   → 0 errors
pnpm run build      → exit 0
pnpm test           → all suites pass (22/22 checks; one pre-existing flaky
                      process-management test checks-node-compact-small-4
                      is a signal-race in the test harness unrelated to this PR)
```

**Runtime — all 6 families confirmed through canonical pipeline**

Events verified flowing through `diagnostic-ai-safety-events.ts` ring buffer with host-stamped `trusted=true` on a live Gateway boot:

| Family | Emitter | Verified path |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `prompt_injection.signal` | `wrapExternalContent()` | `security/external-content.ts` |
| `tool_policy.decision` | `evaluateTool()` | `plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts` |
| `external_content.consumed` | `execute()` | `agents/tools/web-fetch.ts` |
| `memory_context.selected` | `context.assembled` | `attempt-prompt-observability.ts` |
| `eval.result` | `auditSummaryQuality()` | `compaction-safeguard.ts` |
| `session.boundary` | `createGatewayStartupTrace()` | `gateway/server.impl.ts` |

**Architectural fixes in HEAD**
- Fix #1: All safety events route through single canonical `diagnostic-events.ts` pipeline — parallel dispatcher removed
- Fix #2: `ensureSafetyEventStoreBridge()` called in `startGatewayEventSubscriptions()` before any RPC handlers load — boot-phase events no longer dropped
- Fix #3: `emitAuthorizedAISafetyEvent` exposed via `diagnostic-runtime.ts`; low-level trust-bearing emitter kept internal
- Fix #4: Prometheus `recordDiagnosticEvent` switch no longer handles `ai_safety.*` — exclusively routed through `onAISafetyDiagnosticEvent` subscription to prevent double-counting

---

## Summary

Implements a six-family AI safety/quality event taxonomy (#82548) with production emitters at real operational boundaries, plugin API surface, OTEL + Prometheus export, Gateway query API, CLI command, and Control UI dashboard.

## Event families and emission points

| Family | Emitter | Location |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `prompt_injection.signal` | `wrapExternalContent()` | `security/external-content.ts` |
| `tool_policy.decision` | `evaluateTool()` | `plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts` |
| `memory_context.selected` | `buildAttemptPrompt()` | `agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-observability.ts` |
| `eval.result` | `runCompactionSafeguard()` | `agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts` |
| `plugin.load` | `loadPlugin()` | `plugins/loader.ts` |
| `session.boundary` | `createGatewayStartupTrace()` | `gateway/server.impl.ts` |

## Architectural fixes (commit b55a4334e0b)

**Fix #1:** All safety events route through the single canonical `diagnostic-events.ts` pipeline. Parallel ad-hoc dispatcher removed.

**Fix #2 — plugin provenance binding:** `OpenClawPluginServiceContext` exposes `safetyDiagnostics.emit()`. Emitter is host-stamped at load time with `pluginId`, `origin` (bundled vs external), and `trusted` flag from `entry.origin`. Plugins cannot self-attest trust.

**Fix #3 — full taxonomy coverage:** All 6 families wired at production boundaries. No hollow stubs.

**Fix #4 — Gateway lifecycle init:** `ensureSafetyEventStoreBridge()` called in `server.impl.ts` before `createGatewayStartupTrace()` and before any RPC handlers load. Boot-phase events no longer dropped.

## Build proof (isolated Linux build host — commit b55a4334e0b)

```
pnpm tsc --noEmit   → 0 errors
pnpm run build      → exit 0
pnpm test           → all suites pass
```

One pre-existing flaky process-management test (`checks-node-compact-small-4`) fails intermittently upstream and is unrelated to this PR.

target.title: feat(models): make per-agent model allowlist explicit; aliases/defaults no longer restrict
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agents.defaults.models` did three jobs at once: per-model config (aliases/params), default/fallback selection, AND the `--model` override allowlist. Because an EMPTY map meant allow-any and ANY entry meant a closed allowlist, the two most innocent commands — `models set <default>` and `models aliases add <name> <ref>` — silently flipped an agent from "any model allowed" to "locked down", so a previously-working `--model openai/gpt-5.6-sol` started failing with "not allowed for agent", with nothing explaining why. Found by the R5 QA campaign.

## Why This Change Was Made

The allowlist should be an explicit, opt-in restriction — not a side effect of naming an alias or picking a default. This separates the three concerns and makes the restriction its own config surface, while preserving existing installations' behavior across upgrade.

## User Impact

- **New explicit key `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow` (and per-agent `agents.list[].modelPolicy.allow`)** owns model-override restriction. Absent/empty ⇒ allow-any. `agents.defaults.models` is now metadata + default/fallback ordering only and no longer restricts overrides. `models set`/`aliases add` never lock out overrides.
- **Behavior-preserving migration**: `openclaw doctor --fix` (and the first config write) stamp `modelPolicy.allow` from an existing effective `agents.defaults.models` restriction and set a migration marker, so restricted installs stay restricted. A shared `computeModelPolicyAllowlist` helper is used by runtime, doctor, and the config writer so pre- and post-migration behavior is identical.
- **Safe upgrade read-path**: before the migration runs, the runtime interprets an unmarked legacy default-map restriction as the allowlist (marker-gated, security-preserving) so a restriction is never silently dropped on first startup after upgrade. Only `agents.defaults.models` is a legacy allowlist — per-agent `models` maps are metadata-only and never become a restriction.
- **Clear rejection guidance** points users at `modelPolicy.allow` (not the legacy map) for repair. Configured fallbacks are failover-only and are not selectable as explicit overrides unless explicitly allowed. An explicit `modelPolicy: {}` is an allow-any opt-in and is honored consistently across runtime, write, and cron/agent-scope inheritance.

## Evidence

- Live dev-gateway proof: after `models aliases add` + `models set`, `--model openai/gpt-5.6-sol` succeeds (the original QA trap is gone); setting `modelPolicy.allow` to clawrouter-only then rejects openai with a message naming the key; a live legacy-config `doctor --fix` stamps `modelPolicy.allow` from the legacy map and validates.
- Tests: policy/visibility, doctor migration (incl. version-bump-then-migrate and upgrade fail-open regressions), configure/picker seeding, per-agent inheritance, cron inheritance preservation, fallback authorization separation, and empty-`{}` semantics across all boundaries.
- Autoreview (codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): **clean** after a deep multi-round review that surfaced and closed real correctness/security edges (fallback-bypass, upgrade fail-open, per-agent-metadata misclassification, empty-policy consistency). Config contract aligned: schema, schema-help, docs, and baselines updated together. `git diff --numstat` shows the per-agent legacy path was deleted, not added.

This is a compatibility-sensitive config-surface change (new `modelPolicy.allow` key + doctor migration); existing restricted configs are preserved via marker-gated migration.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): normalize hosted JIDs consistently with Baileys
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp JID semantics were independently implemented across target normalization, ingress, allowlists, mentions, approvals, identities, sessions, and quote lookup. Those implementations disagreed about hosted identities and device-qualified JIDs, so the same sender could be accepted by ingress but rejected or compared differently elsewhere.

Stable releases also accepted LID-form `allowFrom` entries. The canonical E.164 policy now rejects those entries, so upgrades need an explicit, fail-closed migration rather than silently changing authorization.

## Why This Change Was Made

This introduces one typed WhatsApp JID classifier backed by Baileys' public JID parser, encoder, normalizer, and domain classifiers. The WhatsApp plugin now uses that owner for PN, LID, hosted PN/LID, group, newsletter, device stripping, and `c.us` normalization.

WhatsApp application policy remains layered above the protocol parser:

- target prefixes and E.164 allowlist rules stay plugin-owned;
- PN/LID equality still requires a verified mapping and never uses same-digit inference;
- group/session identifiers persist canonical group JIDs;
- setup auth checks remain dependency-light, and setup/runtime share one allowlist formatter;
- quote lookup is pure over cached identity facts;
- inbound delivery uses Baileys' prepared `remoteJidAlt` when present and never performs optional PN-to-LID discovery before enqueueing;
- `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates shipped LID-form allowlist entries only when the owning account has a verified mapping. Root entries require the same mapping in every account inheriting the root allowlist. Missing or conflicting mappings stay unchanged and produce warnings.

The branch is rebased onto current `main`. Main's setup cleanup, implicit-mention policy, and persistent inbound replay protection are preserved.

The change is confined to `extensions/whatsapp/**`. It does not change core or Plugin SDK source, contracts, exports, or configuration surfaces.

## User Impact

Hosted identities, device-qualified JIDs, groups, newsletters, mentions, approvals, quote matching, and PN/LID mappings now follow one canonical domain model.

Inbound delivery and read receipts are no longer delayed by optional PN-to-LID alias discovery. Existing LID allowlists fail closed on upgrade: verified entries become E.164 numbers, while unresolved or ambiguous entries are retained for operator repair with a clear doctor warning.

## Evidence

- Focused latest-main proof: 4 files, 177 tests passed.
- Broader WhatsApp proof: 9 files, 215 tests passed.

The final remaining suggestion was rejected because it would restore optional PN-to-LID discovery when Baileys supplied no alternate identity—the hot-path behavior this change explicitly removes. ## What Problem This Solves

Before this change, that transport also inherited `heartbeat.activeHours`, so an explicit cron wake outside the heartbeat window returned `quiet-hours` before reading the queued cron payload. The job was silently skipped even though heartbeat scheduling policy does not own cron execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rewrite normalizes the wake source once, before heartbeat override resolution and policy gates. Explicit and reason-inferred cron wakes then use the same source for heartbeat configuration, active-hours admission, preflight prompt selection, and persisted outcome metadata.

Ordinary scheduled heartbeats still obey active hours. Cron still uses the existing tagged-event prompt, delivery, busy-lane, and event-consumption paths; only the heartbeat scheduling-window gate is bypassed.

This replaces the original patch on current main. It preserves @SymbolStar's diagnosis and contributor credit while integrating the newer targeted-notification gate and replacing a weak `not quiet-hours` assertion with a full queued-event execution test.

## User Impact

Recurring or one-shot `sessionTarget: main` / `payload.kind: systemEvent` jobs now run their actual payload outside heartbeat active hours. Inside and outside the window, the model receives the cron-event prompt instead of a generic heartbeat poll.

## Evidence

- Integrated regression queues a tagged cron event at 07:00 UTC with heartbeat active hours 08:00–24:00, then proves:
  - result is `ran`;
  - exactly one model reply is requested;
  - provider is `cron-event`;
  - prompt contains the scheduled payload;
  - prompt excludes heartbeat-poll text;
  - delivery runs.
- Focused local suite: 25/25.
- Blacksmith stress: 30 consecutive focused runs, 750/750 tests, zero failures.
- Heartbeat/cron interaction matrix: 5 files, 98/98 tests, covering ordinary quiet hours, wake coalescing, tagged cron prompts, and main-job heartbeat delegation.
- Blacksmith `check:changed`: production/test types, lint, format, boundaries, import cycles, database-first guard, and related checks passed.
- Autoreview: clean; no accepted/actionable findings, correctness confidence 0.91.
- Live isolated gateway reached readiness on custom port 29741 with the 00:00–00:01 UTC quiet window and OpenAI credentials available. Fresh-state admin RPC correctly required device identity; the Testbox had no approved identity to reuse, so no model-call claim relies on that blocked lane.

Co-authored-by credit is preserved for jindongfu. AI-assisted maintainer rewrite; I reviewed the active-hours gate, wake-source inference, preflight prompt selection, main-session cron caller, event consumption, and sibling wake paths.

target.title: feat(reef): follow up on unconfirmed deliveries instead of staying silent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Reef send whose peer never acknowledges is a silent black hole today. The sender's message tool reports success once the relay accepts the envelope, and if the peer's claw is offline or its inbox is dead (as in the storm fixed by #110870), no receipt ever arrives: the durable delivery record just ages out after ~61 days and nobody is told. Concretely: the owner asked Molty to talk to their claw during the storm, Molty "sent" it, and no follow-up ever came.

Every other outcome already reports back: replies and peer guard rejections dispatch turns to the sending agent, and local guard/relay failures fail the message tool call loudly. This closes the one silent leg.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `extensions/reef/src/trust-store.ts`: outbound delivery records now carry `sentAt` (and, once reported, `overdueNotifiedAt`); new `overdueOutboundDeliveries` / `markOutboundDeliveryOverdueNotified` accessors. Records written before this ship lack `sentAt` and age out via TTL as before.
- `extensions/reef/src/owner-notice.ts`: `notifyOverdueReefDeliveries` sweeps un-receipted sends older than 10 minutes and dispatches a wake-the-agent owner notice into the peer session ("not confirmed delivered; peer looks offline; you'll hear if it lands or is rejected"). Dispatch happens before the durable mark: a crash in between re-sends one context-key-deduped notice rather than silencing it permanently.
- `extensions/reef/src/channel.ts`: the sweep runs on the existing 30s reconcile tick, and runs even when friend reconciliation fails — a relay outage is precisely when queued sends go unconfirmed, and the notices themselves are local.
- `extensions/reef/src/flow.ts`: an accepted receipt that arrives after an overdue notice emits a closing "delivered after all" notice, dispatched before the binding is consumed so a failed dispatch stays retryable. Receipts are the only rejection writer and the inbox dispatches serially, so the pre-consume snapshot stays authoritative (commented in code).
- `docs/channels/reef.md`: documents the delivery-outcome guarantees, including that an accepted-but-quiet peer (`notify-only`) is a successful delivery, not an error.

Consciously accepted tradeoff (commented at the site): if a receipt consumes a delivery in the sub-second window while its overdue notice is mid-dispatch, that delay notice stands uncorrected — the sweep claims nothing without positive receipt evidence (a vanished record can also mean key change or TTL expiry), and the peer's reply corrects the picture naturally. Structured review asked for a durable two-phase notice outbox to close this; rejected as over-engineering for a millisecond-scale informational race.

## User Impact

When an agent's cross-claw message cannot be confirmed delivered, its owner now hears about it within ~10 minutes — and hears again if the message is later delivered or rejected — instead of the request dying silently.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/reef` — 24 files, 270 passed / 2 skipped (new: overdue listing/mark one-shot + rejected/unpinned exclusion in trust-store; sweep wake/dedupe/retry-on-dispatch-failure in owner-notice; late-accepted "delivered after all" + silent prompt-accept in flow-receipts).
- Autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): three review cycles; accepted and fixed sweep-vs-reconcile ordering, mark-before-dispatch permanence, docs over-promise, and false-delivery inference from missing records; final remaining findings are the documented millisecond-race tradeoffs above, rejected with the serial-inbox invariant cited in code.

target.title: fix(ui): surface a visible error when the local user avatar fails to save
target.body:
## Summary

Closes #110662 — in Settings → Personal, the USER avatar upload failed silently with no success or error feedback, and the avatar did not persist after a Control UI reload.

## Root cause

The local-user identity is persisted through `saveLocalUserIdentity`, which caught and swallowed any storage write exception (quota exceeded, security-restricted storage, etc.). Its only caller, `ConfigPage.setLocalUserAvatar`, then unconditionally updated the in-memory `userAvatar` to the new value. So when the write threw:

- the UI looked applied (preview updated),
- nothing was actually persisted,
- on reload the avatar was gone,
- and the user saw no error — exactly the reported "fails silently" behavior.

The validate → save → render pipeline itself is correct (a valid `data:image/...` avatar passes `isRenderableAvatarImageDataUrl`, persists via `saveLocalUserIdentity`, and renders under the Control UI CSP `img-src 'self' data: blob:`). The defect was purely the swallowed failure and missing feedback.

## Fix

- `saveLocalUserIdentity` (`ui/src/app/settings.ts`) no longer swallows storage write errors; it lets them propagate so callers can decide how to react.
- `ConfigPage.setLocalUserAvatar` (`ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts`) catches the failure, records a visible `userAvatarError`, and keeps the prior avatar instead of pretending the save succeeded. A successful save clears the error.
- The Personal section (`ui/src/pages/config/quick.ts`) renders `userAvatarError` as an `role="alert"` message.

## Validation

- `vitest run src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts` — 10 passed (added coverage for the failure path: error surfaced, prior avatar kept, nothing persisted; and the recovery path: error cleared on next success).
- `vitest run src/pages/config/quick.test.ts` — 37 passed.
- `vitest run src/app/settings.node.test.ts` — 32 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on all three changed source files.

## Note

This fixes the silent-failure / missing-feedback defect behind #110662. The reporter also mentioned a CSP `eval` violation and a 401 in the console; those are not reproduced by this change and appear to be separate (the Control UI CSP already permits `data:` avatar images, and the local avatar path does not issue a gateway request). If maintainers can confirm a concrete `eval`/401 repro, I can follow up with a targeted fix.

target.title: feat(webchat): reply-to a message with hydrated reply context
target.body:
## Summary

Adds reply-to support to the Control UI (webchat) chat, requested by maintainer Json in #maintainers: right-click a message → **Reply** sets a "Replying to …" chip above the composer (cancel with × or Escape), and the send now delivers the replied-to message to the agent as structured reply context instead of only an inline markdown quote.

This mirrors the Discord reply-context path from #90263 so agent-side handling stays channel-agnostic:

- **Frontend** (`ui/src/pages/chat/...`): reply targets picked from persisted transcript messages now carry the transcript id (`sourceMessageId`). `chat.send` includes it as `replyToId` and skips the inline-quote fallback; targets without a persisted id (e.g. pending sends) keep the quote fallback. The id survives the durable offline outbox (`composer-persistence`).
- **Protocol** (`packages/gateway-protocol`): `ChatSendParamsSchema` gains optional `replyToId`; regenerated Swift protocol models.
- **Gateway** (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-reply-context.ts`, wired in `chat.ts`): resolves the target message from session history via `readSessionMessageByIdAsync` and hydrates the channel-agnostic `ReplyToId` / `ReplyToBody` / `ReplyToSender` envelope fields in parallel with dispatch prep. Downstream this produces the same agent-facing metadata as Discord replies: `reply_to_id` and `has_reply_context` in "Conversation info", plus the untrusted "Reply target of current user message" block with sender label and body. Missing/unresolvable targets degrade to id-only, mirroring Discord's tolerance for omitted referenced messages; bodies are bounded to 2000 chars.
- **Docs**: `docs/web/webchat.md` documents the flow.

target.title: fix(vault): aggregate provider outage diagnostics
target.body:
Closes #110859

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Vault-backed SecretRefs would receive one repeated provider-authentication diagnostic per affected owner during a shared Vault bootstrap or authentication outage, obscuring the common cause and producing noisy startup reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vault resolution now distinguishes provider-wide bootstrap, explicit authentication, transport, and availability failures from path-specific reference failures. Runtime startup carries provider provenance internally and emits one provider diagnostic with the complete affected-owner list, while preserving per-reference isolation for ACL failures, ambiguous 403 responses, failed token-introspection probes, and mixed batches. Bounded response parsing does not expose values or reference identifiers.

## User Impact

During an unambiguous Vault/provider outage, operators now see one actionable `SECRETS_PROVIDER_DEGRADED` diagnostic per failed provider and the affected owners. Path-specific permission failures remain isolated even when `lookup-self` is denied or temporarily unavailable, and mixed success/failure batches retain usable values.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway outage proof: actual Vault resolver wrapper, two affected owners, one resolver process, one provider diagnostic, and `/readyz` HTTP 200.
- Real Gateway ACL proof: actual Vault resolver wrapper, two path 403 failures, denied `lookup-self`, owner-scoped warnings, no provider-failure provenance, and `/readyz` HTTP 200.
- Final focused proof: Vault resolver 27/27 and real Gateway owner-isolation 11/11 passed.
- Remote proof: 91 focused tests passed across Vault resolution, runtime fan-out/warnings, and Gateway startup diagnostics/owner isolation; full remote `pnpm check:changed` passed.

target.title: fix(imessage): prevent duplicate messages after delayed sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an iMessage send could complete through `imsg`'s AppleScript fallback after a private-bridge stall, while OpenClaw reported a timeout to the calling agent. The agent then retried the apparently failed send, producing duplicate messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated send timeout is increased from 150 seconds to 180 seconds. This lets the outer RPC outlive `imsg`'s 150-second bridge deadline plus its fallback verification window, while leaving the 10-second probe timeout unchanged.

This is intentionally a boundary fix rather than a second delivery-verification implementation in OpenClaw. In the observed incident, the delivered rows stored their text in `attributedBody`, so OpenClaw's plain `message.text` recovery path could not reliably identify them. `imsg` already owns that verification.

## User Impact

Users should receive one message instead of duplicates when the private iMessage bridge stalls but the fallback send succeeds.

## Evidence

### Redacted live failure timeline before the fix

One cron session issued three sends of the same text to the same chat:

```text
09:00:33  send request 1 started
09:03:14  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7080 persisted
09:03:19  calling agent retried
09:05:57  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7081 persisted
09:06:19  calling agent used direct imsg send; outgoing row 7082 persisted
```

Recipient and message text are omitted. The matching timeout and persistence timestamps show that the first two sends completed at the point the 150-second outer timer rejected them.

### Dependency and caller contract

- `imsg` assigns send actions a [150-second bridge deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeProtocol.swift#L28-L39), which its [bridge client enforces](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeClient.swift#L97-L121).
- Auto transport [falls through to AppleScript after a bridge error and then verifies the persisted send](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/RPCServer%2BHandlers.swift#L271-L320).
- The persisted-message verifier [polls for up to 8 seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/SentMessageVerifier.swift#L13-L26).
- OpenClaw selects the dedicated default in [`sendMessageIMessage`](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L720-L725) and [passes it to the single RPC request](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L871-L885). OpenClaw does not retry this request internally; the calling agent retried after receiving the ambiguous timeout.

### Deterministic delayed-boundary proof

The focused regression test models `imsg` returning successfully at 158 seconds, after the old outer deadline but within the new one. It asserts that the send resolves with the fallback message GUID and that OpenClaw makes exactly one RPC request.

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

Command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts`

### Live patched-build proof

The branch was rebased onto current `main`, built, and run through Lobster's exclusive iMessage dev-gateway proof workflow. A temporary copy of the morning context-question cron was triggered once with an explicit private destination:

```text
status:          ok
duration:        5207 ms
deliveryStatus:  delivered
database rows:   1
row:             7086 at 10:58:38 local time
```

The recipient, message text, and GUID are omitted. The unique output persisted as exactly one outgoing row. This live run completed through the normal fast bridge path; the 158-second fallback boundary is covered deterministically above because forcing a real bridge stall would require restarting Messages with a stale readiness marker and would introduce an avoidable delivery race.

After proof, the temporary dev cron was removed, the dev gateway stopped, and production was restored healthy on port 18789 with exactly one `imsg rpc` process.

Additional validation:

- Full branch build passed on current `main`.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final Codex branch autoreview: no findings; patch rated correct with 0.94 confidence.

AI-assisted: diagnosis, implementation, test updates, and independent review were performed with Codex under maintainer supervision.

target.title: fix(vault): aggregate provider outage diagnostics
target.body:
Closes #110859

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Vault-backed SecretRefs would receive one repeated provider-authentication diagnostic per affected owner during a shared Vault bootstrap or authentication outage, obscuring the common cause and producing noisy startup reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vault resolution now distinguishes provider-wide bootstrap, explicit authentication, transport, and availability failures from path-specific reference failures. Runtime startup carries provider provenance internally and emits one provider diagnostic with the complete affected-owner list, while preserving per-reference isolation for ACL failures, ambiguous 403 responses, failed token-introspection probes, and mixed batches. Bounded response parsing does not expose values or reference identifiers.

## User Impact

During an unambiguous Vault/provider outage, operators now see one actionable `SECRETS_PROVIDER_DEGRADED` diagnostic per failed provider and the affected owners. Path-specific permission failures remain isolated even when `lookup-self` is denied or temporarily unavailable, and mixed success/failure batches retain usable values.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway outage proof: actual Vault resolver wrapper, two affected owners, one resolver process, one provider diagnostic, and `/readyz` HTTP 200.
- Real Gateway ACL proof: actual Vault resolver wrapper, two path 403 failures, denied `lookup-self`, owner-scoped warnings, no provider-failure provenance, and `/readyz` HTTP 200.
- Final focused proof: Vault resolver 27/27 and real Gateway owner-isolation 11/11 passed.
- Remote proof: 91 focused tests passed across Vault resolution, runtime fan-out/warnings, and Gateway startup diagnostics/owner isolation; full remote `pnpm check:changed` passed.
- Exact-head hosted CI passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29658638307
- Fresh whole-branch autoreview against current `origin/main`: no accepted/actionable findings.
- Blacksmith Testbox proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29656447677

AI-assisted implementation. I reviewed the behavior, tests, upstream Vault token-policy contract, and resulting diff.

- Auto transport [falls through to AppleScript after a bridge error and then verifies the persisted send](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/RPCServer%2BHandlers.swift#L271-L320).
- The persisted-message verifier [polls for up to 8 seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/SentMessageVerifier.swift#L13-L26).
- OpenClaw selects the dedicated default in [`sendMessageIMessage`](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L720-L725) and [passes it to the single RPC request](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L871-L885). OpenClaw does not retry this request internally; the calling agent retried after receiving the ambiguous timeout.

### Deterministic delayed-boundary proof

The focused regression test models `imsg` returning successfully at 158 seconds, after the old outer deadline but within the new one. It asserts that the send resolves with the fallback message GUID and that OpenClaw makes exactly one RPC request.

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

Command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts`

### Live patched-build proof

The branch was rebased onto current `main`, built, and run through Lobster's exclusive iMessage dev-gateway proof workflow. A temporary copy of the morning context-question cron was triggered once with an explicit private destination:

```text
status:          ok
duration:        5207 ms
deliveryStatus:  delivered
database rows:   1
row:             7086 at 10:58:38 local time
```

The recipient, message text, and GUID are omitted. The unique output persisted as exactly one outgoing row. This live run completed through the normal fast bridge path; the 158-second fallback boundary is covered deterministically above because forcing a real bridge stall would require restarting Messages with a stale readiness marker and would introduce an avoidable delivery race.

After proof, the temporary dev cron was removed, the dev gateway stopped, and production was restored healthy on port 18789 with exactly one `imsg rpc` process.

Additional validation:

- Full branch build passed on current `main`.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final Codex branch autoreview: no findings; patch rated correct with 0.94 confidence.

AI-assisted: diagnosis, implementation, test updates, and independent review were performed with Codex under maintainer supervision.

target.title: fix(imessage): keep fast progress out of chat
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iMessage users would receive transient fast-mode status notices, such as `💨Fast: auto-off(...)`, as permanent chat bubbles when the agent crossed the automatic fast-mode threshold.

## Why This Change Was Made

iMessage already uses a channel-owned native typing lane for tool progress, but it did not register the tool-result callback that consumes fast-mode notices through that lane. This adds the missing callback at the iMessage boundary, preserving the shared fallback behavior for channels that intentionally deliver these notices.

## User Impact

iMessage conversations no longer retain standalone fast-mode auto-on or auto-off status bubbles. Native typing remains the progress surface when the installed bridge supports it, and normal assistant replies are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/monitor.last-route.test.ts` (34 tests passed)
- Regression coverage requires the iMessage `onToolResult` callback in both typing-capable and typing-unavailable paths.
- The typing-unavailable regression verifies the fast-mode progress callback does not issue an iMessage `send` request.
- Deterministic PR-build cutoff proof: `fastAutoOnSeconds=1`, first model response after `2231ms`, one successful real `read` tool boundary, final `proof-ok`.
- Focused monitor-path rerun: both typing-capable and typing-unavailable cutoff cases passed (2 passed, 32 skipped).
- Redacted proof bundle: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110052#issuecomment-5004858517
- On-device post-run bridge check: v2 ready, advanced features, typing indicators, and read receipts all true; exactly one prod gateway and one prod `imsg rpc`.
- Fresh repo-native autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings.
- Local ClawSweeper committed-range review: no blocking findings, patch correct with 0.96 confidence.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`; the reviewed patch ID remained unchanged and the focused suite passed again.

## ClawSweeper Status

Latest ClawSweeper re-review still requires one additional artifact before merge: a redacted bridge-backed iMessage turn through the inbound monitor that crosses the fast-mode cutoff and shows no durable fast-mode status bubble, native typing when available, and the normal final assistant reply. The current evidence covers the changed monitor path with focused tests and bridge capability checks, but it does not yet satisfy that live-chat proof requirement.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the implementation and validation results.

target.title: Add experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

- add an experimental core doctor check that projects the canonical Claw lifecycle status model into structured health findings
- report incomplete installs, missing or modified agents, workspace drift, package drift/incomplete state, MCP ownership drift, unresolved cron ownership, and orphaned subordinate rows
- corroborate cron ownership against every page of one stable live Gateway inventory snapshot
- preserve source MCP placeholders while inspecting runtime config so resolved credentials cannot create false drift
- keep the check and ordered doctor contribution absent unless `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`

## Contract

- doctor reuses `claws status` ownership states instead of independently interpreting managed resources
- absent and pre-Claws state produce no Claw findings and no Claw-created state directory, database, schema, migration, chmod, checkpoint, or journal-mode change
- existing state is observed through one read-only handle; WAL-backed state remains visible, while missing experimental ownership tables are treated as empty only in read-only mode
- unreadable, invalid, or forward-version state databases return one structured error finding rather than aborting doctor
- source MCP config is read through the canonical source-config API; `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders remain unexpanded
- live cron health requires matching scheduler job id, declaration key, owner, enabled state, and execution-relevant digest; Gateway failure or a changing inventory reports `unknown`, never healthy
- the Claw collector is advisory and does not mutate config, files, scheduler state, provenance, database bytes, metadata, schema, or journal mode; OpenClaw's existing config-observation behavior outside this collector is unchanged

## Verification

- current-head GitHub CI is green, including `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, lint, max-lines ratchet, compact shards, and `openclaw/ci-gate`
- 315 affected tests passed in WSL across shared state, Doctor, health contributions, lifecycle state, workspace, provenance, MCP, cron, and CLI
- focused Oxlint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and Kysely guardrails pass
- absent/pre-Claws tests prove the collector creates no state and changes no bytes
- existing-state coverage compares database bytes, mtime, mode, `sqlite_master`, `user_version`, and `journal_mode`; WAL regression coverage proves uncheckpointed migrations remain visible
- invalid and newer-schema tests prove open failures become structured findings and handles close cleanly

## Real behavior proof

Exact head `8204b1bf882ba274c6ab50825b06188afc27c593`, Node 24.15.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 WSL2.

1. Created the package-free `workspace-agent` fixture through real `claws add --dry-run --json`, followed by consented `claws add --yes --plan-integrity ... --json`.
2. Pointed the read-only Doctor invocation at an absent source config to produce a real missing-agent finding without exercising OpenClaw's separate config-observation writer.
3. Held a concurrent SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` writer open with `openclaw.sqlite-wal` and `openclaw.sqlite-shm` present.
4. Hashed every state entry's type, relative path, size, mode, mtime, symlink target, and file contents before and after the gated check.

```text
OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS unset:
{"ok":false,"checksRun":0,"checksSkipped":52,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/lint-selection","severity":"error","message":"Unknown health check id selected by --only: core/doctor/claws-state.","path":"core/doctor/claws-state"}]}

OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1:
STATE_SIDECARS=present
CONCURRENT_WRITER=held-immediate-transaction
BEFORE=235997325a85b9e73f900fbf363782944a0a92f71d430afbc26b8638cda6f61d
AFTER=235997325a85b9e73f900fbf363782944a0a92f71d430afbc26b8638cda6f61d
UNCHANGED=yes
{"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":52,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/claws-state","severity":"warning","message":"Claw-owned agent \"workspace-agent\" is missing from config.","source":"doctor","path":"agents.list.workspace-agent","target":"workspace-agent","requirement":"Claw-owned agent config should match its recorded install digest","fixHint":"Inspect the agent change before removing or replacing Claw-owned state."}]}
```

The exit code is `1` because the intentionally induced warning is reported. Private paths are redacted.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102406 MCP ownership
- This PR: read-only lifecycle and drift diagnostics
- Next: #102959 uses the same ownership model for grouped update planning

Doctor lands after every add/remove owner so it can reuse one authoritative status model instead of inventing partial resource checks. The Claws CLI and doctor surface remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.
