target.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a browser navigation or action invalidates the selected raw target, `resolveTargetIdAfterNavigate` retried once and then adopted **any** sole remaining tab, regardless of whether that tab matched the acted-on page:

```ts
if (options?.allowSingleTabFallback && tabs.length === 1) {
  return { targetId: tabs[0]?.targetId ?? opts.oldTargetId, shouldRetry: false };
}
```

The shared resolver backs both `/navigate` and `/act`. So if an action closed or replaced the selected target while an unrelated tab stayed open at a different URL, `/act` could return that unrelated tab's `targetId`. A caller that trusts the response then continues its next mutating action on the wrong page. The focused test even asserted this: old target `old-123`, sole unrelated tab `only-tab` at a different URL, expected result `only-tab`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sole-tab adoption, tab ordering, and a bare URL match are not proof of identity. The response target must be the backend-owned identity of the page that actually executed the operation. When that identity is gone and continuity cannot be proven, the resolver should return the acted-on (now stale or closed) identity so the caller requires a fresh selection, rather than guessing a tab.

The codebase already draws this distinction elsewhere: the post-interaction navigation guard separates newly-appeared tabs from pre-existing ones by their initial target ids, and default tab selection returns `null` ("require a fresh explicit choice") when a sticky target disappears without a proven migration. This change brings the post-action resolver up to the same standard.

## User Impact

A replacement is now adopted only when continuity is provable:

- **Provable replacement (with a pre-action snapshot):** the acted-on page was replaced by a target that did **not** exist before the operation. Exactly one such newly-appeared target is adopted. A pre-existing unrelated tab is never adopted, which fixes the reported wrong-tab routing.
- **Provable renderer swap (navigate path):** exactly one candidate now sits at the URL we just navigated to (Chrome detaches the old renderer target and reattaches the same tab under a new raw target). URL equality is trusted only against the just-navigated URL, never a stale pre-action URL, tab ordering, or a sole remaining tab.
- **Unproven:** the backend-owned acted-on identity is returned so the caller re-selects.

The `/act` route now snapshots tab ids just before the Playwright action and passes them to the resolver. Prior continuity is preserved: `chrome-extension://` to HTTPS navigation (#25323 / #25326) and action-triggered target replacement (#46137) still resolve to the correct replacement.

## Evidence

### Live browser proof (real Chrome over CDP)

A standalone harness (`extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.mts`) launches a real Chrome instance and reads its live targets through `Target.getTargets`, the same CDP surface the plugin's `listTabs` uses. The genuine raw target ids and URLs are fed into the shipped `resolveTargetIdAfterNavigate`. Nothing is mocked; URLs are redacted in the transcript.

Run:

```
pnpm exec tsx extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.mts
```

Redacted output:

```
=== Live-browser proof for #103785 (real Chrome over CDP) ===

Scenario A: action closes acted-on tab A; unrelated tab B survives

  pre-action targets (real CDP):
    - target=48DEEFC6… url=data:<UNRELATED-B>
    - target=19F1C22F… url=data:<ACTED-ON-A>
  post-action targets (real CDP):
    - target=48DEEFC6… url=data:<UNRELATED-B>

  resolver returned target=19F1C22F… (A=19F1C22F…, B=48DEEFC6…)
  kept acted-on identity A: true
  adopted unrelated survivor B: false
  PASS: unrelated survivor B was NOT adopted.

Scenario B: renderer swap (old raw target detached, page reattaches at navigated url)

  pre-navigate targets (real CDP):
    - target=7AC30457… url=data:<PRE-SWAP>
  post-navigate targets (real CDP):
    - target=F4202B71… url=data:<SWAPPED>

  resolver returned target=F4202B71… (old=7AC30457…, reattached=F4202B71…)
  adopted reattached target at navigated url: true
  PASS: renderer-swap continuity preserved.

=== ALL SCENARIOS PASSED ===
```

- **Scenario A (the reported bug):** tab A is acted on and closed while an unrelated tab B stays open. After the action only B remains, yet the resolver returns A's backend-owned identity and never adopts B. Before this change the sole-tab fallback would have returned B and routed the next action onto the wrong page.
- **Scenario B (continuity preserved):** the acted-on raw target is detached and the page reattaches under a new raw target at the just-navigated URL. The resolver adopts the reattached target, so renderer-swap / action-triggered replacement paths keep working.

### Source and test changes

- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot-target.ts`: removed the sole-tab fallback; adopt only a uniquely newly-appeared target, or the single candidate at the just-navigated URL.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts`: capture pre-action target ids (reusing the existing-session `initialTabTargetIds`, and a new snapshot for the Playwright path) and pass them as `knownTargetIds`.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts`: the "sole unrelated tab" case now asserts the acted-on identity is kept; added a regression test for a sole tab matching only a stale URL.

Automated tests (focused + full browser extension suite):

```
pnpm test:extension browser -- extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts
# Test Files 2 passed (2) | Tests 34 passed (34)

pnpm test:extension browser
# Tests 1887 passed | 1 skipped
# (the only failure, doctor-browser "skips Chrome auto-detection", also fails on a clean checkout: it depends on a local Chrome install)
```

Extension package boundary typecheck: `extension package boundary check passed`.

Closes #103785

**Problem**: When an agent ID contains a colon (e.g., `copilot:agent`), the inline session key parsing via `row.key.split(":")[1]` truncates the agent ID at the first colon. target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body in crabline injection
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109992

**What changed**: Added `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the `postCrablineInbound()` error path. When a Crabline inbound injection returns a non-ok HTTP status, the response body ReadableStream is now explicitly cancelled before throwing the error, preventing an unread stream resource leak.

**What NOT changed**: No change to the happy path — successful responses still pass through to the complete handler as before. No change to the Crabline injection logic, request construction, or error message format. No new dependencies added.

**merge-risk**: Minimal — the pattern `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` is a standard no-op on success and a no-throw guard on failure. It affects only the single error path in `crabline-transport.ts`. Zero risk of regression on the ok path.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a Crabline inbound injection HTTP request returns a non-ok response (e.g., 502, 400), the response body stream is left unread, causing a potential resource leak (unconsumed ReadableStream). Node.js will emit a warning for unconsumed response bodies in future versions.

**Root Cause**: `postCrablineInbound()` throws immediately in the `if (!response.ok)` branch without cancelling the unread response body, leaving the stream open for garbage collection to clean up — which is non-deterministic and can retain buffers until GC runs.

**Solution**: Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the error path to eagerly release the stream. The `cancel()` method (Fetch API standard) releases the stream's resources. The `?.` optional chaining guards against a null body (e.g., 204 No Content responses or server errors that omit a body). The `.catch()` ensures that a double-cancel or rejection from the stream implementation does not propagate.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: When a Crabline inbound injection receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 502, 400), the response body stream is now explicitly cancelled before the error is thrown, eliminating a resource leak from an unconsumed ReadableStream.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw 2026.7.2, Vitest 4.1.10

target.title: fix(openai-http): keep SSE argument chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

Replace `String.prototype.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` in `splitArgumentsForStreaming` to prevent SSE argument chunks from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. The old code could produce invalid JSON when multi-byte characters (e.g., CJK, emoji) straddled the 256-char chunk boundary, causing downstream parse failures on the client.

Fixes #110642

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: SSE streaming chunks of tool_call arguments can contain truncated/invalid UTF-16 when the 256-char boundary falls inside a surrogate pair, causing the client to receive malformed JSON.

**Root Cause**: `splitArgumentsForStreaming()` in `src/gateway/openai-http.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` which operates on UTF-16 code units without awareness of surrogate pairs. When a multi-byte character spans positions 255-256, the slice produces a broken chunk.

**Solution**: Import and use `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, which ensures surrogate pairs are never split. The loop increment is changed from a fixed `+= chunkSize` to `+= chunk.length` (with `|| 1` fallback) because the safe slice may return 256 or 257 characters.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: SSE chunking of tool_call arguments to not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic / vitest 4.1.10 / OpenClaw worktree

target.title: fix(gateway): trim device.pair approve/reject requestId
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`device.pair.approve` / `device.pair.reject` used `requestId` as pasted, while
the same module already trims `deviceId` and `gateway.suspend.prepare` trims
`requestId`. Clipboard padding produced false `unknown requestId` for a live
pending pair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trim `requestId` once at the start of both handlers before pending-lookup /
approve / reject / broadcast, matching the suspend prepare contract.

## User Impact

**Before:** Approving/rejecting with `" req-… "` failed as unknown.

**After:** Surrounding whitespace is ignored; the pending pairing key still
matches.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/server-methods/devices.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/devices.test.ts`
- Production path: `deviceHandlers["device.pair.approve"|"device.pair.reject"]`
  → `requestId.trim()` → `approveDevicePairing` / `rejectDevicePairing`
- Compatibility: stored pending keys remain unpadded; only the RPC input is
  normalized

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Live Gateway: plant a pending device pairing in an isolated state DB, then
`device.pair.reject` with a padded `requestId` rejects that pending request.
A padded unknown id still returns `unknown requestId`.

### Canonical reachability path

Gateway RPC `device.pair.reject` → trim `requestId` →
`rejectDevicePairing(trimmed)` → respond success with trimmed id

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Same `.trim()` pattern as `gateway.suspend.prepare` (`suspend.ts`) and local
`deviceId.trim()` checks; no new config.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` /
config / `HOME`; loopback Gateway; pending request planted via
`requestDevicePairing` into the same state dir before Gateway start.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# plant pending into OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, then:
node scripts/run-node.mjs devices list --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway call device.pair.reject \
  --params '{"requestId":" <pending-request-id> "}' \
  --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
```

### Evidence after fix

Pending list (redacted):

```json
{
  "pending": [
    {
      "requestId": "c89c6c7c-3264-4e6b-8466-91ed2893087d",
      "deviceId": "proof-device-1",
      "role": "node"
    }
  ],
  "paired": []
}
```

Padded reject succeeds (trimmed id echoed):

```json
{
  "requestId": "c89c6c7c-3264-4e6b-8466-91ed2893087d",
  "deviceId": "proof-device-1"
}
```

Unknown padded id:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "unknown requestId"
  }
}
```

Gateway log also showed a padded approve attempt resolving the same pending
request before role-policy denial (`role-management-requires-admin`), which
confirms lookup-after-trim on the approve path as well.

### Observed result after fix

A padded pending pairing `requestId` resolves through a real Gateway WebSocket
`device.pair.reject` call.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

target.title: fix(gateway): trim cron job ids before exact lookup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveCronJobId` returned `params.id ?? params.jobId` without trimming, while
nearby cron wake paths already trim `sessionKey` / `agentId`. Padded job ids
made `cron.get` / `cron.run` / `cron.remove` / `cron.update` / `cron.runs`
report not found for existing jobs. `cron.update` also bypassed the helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trim inside `resolveCronJobId` and route `cron.update` through that helper so
every exact job-id lookup shares one normalization point.

## User Impact

**Before:** `" ${jobId} "` failed as missing/not found.

**After:** Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped before store lookup.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts`
- Production path: `cronHandlers` get/run/remove/update/runs →
  `resolveCronJobId` → `context.cron.readJob` / `enqueueRun`
- Compatibility: whitespace-only ids still count as missing

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Live Gateway RPC: create a cron job, then `cron.get` with a padded id returns
the job. Whitespace-only id still returns `INVALID_REQUEST` / missing id.

### Canonical reachability path

`openclaw gateway call cron.get` → `resolveCronJobId` (trim) →
`context.cron.readJob(<trimmed>)` → job payload

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Local helper only; aligns with existing cron wake `.trim()` usage; no new
config.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` /
config / `HOME`; loopback Gateway via `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run`;
Node 22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# isolated gateway + token on a free loopback port
node scripts/run-node.mjs cron add --name trim-proof --every 1h --session main \
  --system-event "trim proof heartbeat" --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway call cron.get \
  --params '{"id":" <job-id> "}' --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway call cron.get \
  --params '{"id":"   "}' --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
```

### Evidence after fix

Redacted live RPC (padded id succeeds):

```json
{
  "id": "24df4718-c0b2-477a-ac33-2d8e1c348684",
  "name": "trim-proof",
  "enabled": true,
  "schedule": { "kind": "every", "everyMs": 3600000 },
  "sessionTarget": "main",
  "payload": { "kind": "systemEvent", "text": "trim proof heartbeat" }
}
```

Whitespace-only id:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "invalid cron.get params: missing id"
  }
}
```

### Observed result after fix

A padded existing cron job id resolves through a real Gateway WebSocket
`cron.get` call; whitespace-only input remains invalid.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): notify users when Codex session changes
target.body:
Related: #106957, #108769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channel users could receive no reply when another gateway or session transition superseded the Codex session generation before their message ran. The agent runner logged `Embedded agent failed before reply`, but the generation error was treated as generic; normal group failure policy then converted the reply to `NO_REPLY`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify the stable Codex generation-fence error as a known terminal failure and return a short, redacted retry prompt. This is intentionally not a durable-ingress retry: the channel claim is completed when the turn is adopted, before Codex starts, and replaying an adopted turn can duplicate side effects. The same in-flight turn also keeps the stale physical session ID, so retrying that run cannot reclaim the authoritative generation.

Codex app-server identifies resume/start operations by thread ID and rejoins running threads only inside its current process; it exposes no cross-process generation token. OpenClaw therefore continues to own and enforce this fence. See [`ThreadResumeParams`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b8b61bc692517adcd18622df260f2ddd80635122/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L310-L324), [`TurnStartParams`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b8b61bc692517adcd18622df260f2ddd80635122/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L71-L75), and the process-local running-thread lookup in [`thread_processor.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b8b61bc692517adcd18622df260f2ddd80635122/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L3296-L3344).

## User Impact

Instead of silence, users now receive: `⚠️ This Codex session changed before your message could run. Please send it again.` The physical session identifier is never exposed. The underlying generation fence and no-replay behavior are unchanged.

Release-note context: fixes silent channel drops when a Codex session generation changes before an adopted turn starts.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxv416r7z3df45ydepkhzvy7`: focused terminal-failure suite passed 20/20; full changed gate passed (format, boundaries, production/test typechecks, lint, and guards). [Run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29653800465)
- Regression covers a Telegram group turn, asserts a non-silent final reply, exact actionable copy, and session-ID redaction.
- Fresh uncommitted autoreview: clean, correctness confidence 0.97.
- Live two-gateway/channel proof was not run: no deterministic source-blind fixture exists without an approved private channel or internal state injection.

AI-assisted: implementation and review performed with Codex.

Fixes an issue where Nextcloud Talk room lookup receives a non-2xx response and leaves its unread response body open while resolving inbound room metadata.

target.title: fix(doctor): bound session snapshot store reads with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor session-snapshot scan/repair loaded session store JSON with unbounded
`fs.readFileSync` at two call sites. A corrupted or hostile multi-GB
`sessions.json` under the user state directory could OOM `openclaw doctor`
before JSON parse or repair logic ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a shared `readSnapshotStoreRaw` helper with `statSync` +
`MAX_SNAPSHOT_STORE_BYTES = 16 MiB`, and route both the scan loader and the
repair backup read through it. Oversized stores fail closed: doctor emits an
operator-visible Session snapshots note, structured health issues use
`kind: "store-too-large"`, and repair effects record
`would-skip-oversized-session-store`.

## User Impact

**Before:** An oversized session store could force an unbounded sync string
alloc during doctor snapshot health, or be skipped silently with no operator
signal.

**After:** Stores above 16 MiB are rejected before `readFileSync`. Doctor
reports the skip, and normal stores continue to scan/repair.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.ts`,
  `src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts`
- Production path: `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` /
  `noteSessionSnapshotHealth` → `loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` /
  repair `updateSessionStore` callback → `readSnapshotStoreRaw`
- Compatibility: normal stores unchanged; oversized stores are skipped with a
  warning instead of crashing the process

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

A ~17 MiB session store is not passed to `readFileSync`. Isolated
`openclaw doctor --non-interactive --yes` prints a Session snapshots note that
the store was skipped as oversized.

### Canonical reachability path

`openclaw doctor` → session snapshot health →
`noteSessionSnapshotHealth` / `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` →
`loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` → `readSnapshotStoreRaw` (stat + 16 MiB cap)
→ skip + warn on overflow

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Same bound pattern as other doctor store caps; no new config/env keys.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; Node 22.23.1; isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `HOME` under `/tmp` with a
planted 17 MiB `sessions.json`; CLI via
`node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes` after local build.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
PROOF=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-doctor-snap-proof-XXXXXX)
STATE=$PROOF/state; HOME_DIR=$PROOF/home; CONFIG=$PROOF/openclaw.json
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR" "$STATE/agents/main/sessions"
printf '%s\n' '{"agents":{"list":[{"id":"main","default":true}]}}' > "$CONFIG"
# write 17 MiB of bytes to $STATE/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
HOME=$HOME_DIR OPENCLAW_HOME=$HOME_DIR OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE \
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$CONFIG CI=true \
  node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes
```

Focused regression:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts \
  -t "oversized session stores" --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Redacted CLI:

```text
◇  Session snapshots ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - Skipped oversized session store                                                    │
│    .../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json                                       │
│    (.../sessions.json: file too large (17825792 bytes, max 16777216)).                │
│    Snapshot-path health was not scanned.                                              │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Focused tests:

```text
✓ reports oversized session stores without reading them into memory
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 24 skipped (25)
```

### Observed result after fix

Real `openclaw doctor` warns and skips the oversized store; `readFileSync` is
never called for that path during snapshot scan.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

`audit.list` / `audit.activity.list` forwarded `agentId`, `sessionKey`, and
`runId` into exact store filters without trimming. A pasted filter like
`" main "` produced a successful empty page even when matching events existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize those exact-match filters with `normalizeOptionalString` before
`listAuditEvents`, matching the same file's existing cursor `.trim()` behavior
and other gateway list filters.

## User Impact

**Before:** Padded filter ids returned empty success results.

**After:** Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped so padded filters hit the
same rows as the canonical ids.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.trim.store.test.ts`
- Production path: gateway `audit.list` / `audit.activity.list` handlers →
  normalized filters → `listAuditEvents`
- Compatibility: empty/whitespace-only filters still omit the field

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. Untrimmed store filters miss a planted row (`agentId: " main "` → empty).
2. Production `audit.list` with the same padded filters returns the planted
   `agent.run.finished` event after handler-side trim.

### Canonical reachability path

Real SQLite audit store (`recordAuditEvent`) → Gateway handler
`auditHandlers["audit.list"]` → `normalizeOptionalString` → `listAuditEvents`
(default `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`) → respond with matching events

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `@openclaw/normalization-core/string-coerce` `normalizeOptionalString`;
no new config/env.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted checkout; temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; real OpenClaw state SQLite
audit table (not a mocked `listAuditEvents`). Node via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/audit.trim.store.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
✓ returns the planted run for padded agentId/runId filters 331ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Negative control: `listAuditEvents({ filters: { agentId: " main ", runId: " run-trim-1 " } })`
returns `[]`. After-fix handler call with the same padded params returns the
planted `agentId: "main"` / `runId: "run-trim-1"` event.

### Observed result after fix

Padded audit filter ids resolve through the production gateway handler against
a real stored audit event.

### What was not tested

Live multi-operator Gateway WebSocket session against a long-lived production
state DB. Proof uses the production handler + real SQLite store under an
isolated state dir.

### Fix classification

bugfix — exact-match filter paste/padding miss

target.title: fix(doctor): stream JSONL line counts without full-file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` state integrity counted main-session JSONL transcript lines by
`fs.readFileSync` + walking every character. A multi-hundred-MB transcript forced
the whole file into one UTF-8 string before the `lineCount <= 1` warning could
run, so doctor could spike RSS to roughly the transcript size.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the full-file string read with a fixed-size sync chunk reader
(`openSync` + `readSync`) that counts `0x0a` bytes and preserves the old
trailing-newline rule for the final incomplete line. Close failures stay inside
the helper so an uncommon `closeSync` error cannot abort doctor after a
successful count.

## User Impact

**Before:** A large main transcript could make `openclaw doctor` allocate a
full-file string just to count lines. A close failure after chunked counting
could also abort the doctor command.

**After:** Line counting streams 64 KiB chunks, so doctor keeps the
single-line warning without buffering the whole transcript, and close errors
remain fail-soft.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts`,
  `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts`
- Production path: `noteStateIntegrity` → main transcript exists →
  `countJsonlLines(transcriptPath)` → `lineCount <= 1` warning
- Compatibility: empty / missing / single-line / multi-line semantics unchanged;
  only the read strategy and close fail-soft boundary change

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Isolated `openclaw doctor --non-interactive --yes` against a one-line main
transcript prints the State integrity warning; the same command against an
8 × 64 KiB multi-chunk transcript does not.

### Canonical reachability path

`openclaw doctor` → `noteStateIntegrity` → resolve main session transcript →
`countJsonlLines` (chunked `readSync`) → optional
`Main session transcript has only … line` warning

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Local to doctor state integrity; no new config/env surface. Chunk size matches
the existing doctor JSONL reader constant family (64 KiB).

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; Node 22.23.1; isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `HOME` under `/tmp`; CLI via
`node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes` after local build.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# one-line
PROOF=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-doctor-jsonl-proof-XXXXXX)
STATE=$PROOF/state; HOME_DIR=$PROOF/home; CONFIG=$PROOF/openclaw.json
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR" "$STATE/agents/main/sessions"
printf '%s\n' '{"agents":{"list":[{"id":"main","default":true}]}}' > "$CONFIG"
printf '%s' '{"type":"session"}' > "$STATE/agents/main/sessions/short-main.jsonl"
```

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI mock has limited curated chat state for design QA, so reviewers have to rely on ad hoc sessions when checking empty chat, longer transcripts, markdown rendering, code blocks, tables, warnings, and recoverable error copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds stable dev/mock-only fixture sessions to the Control UI mock server. The proposed fixtures cover a New session empty state, a coding session, a response-shape showcase, and a markdown showcase without changing production gateway or session APIs.

## User Impact

There is no production user-facing behavior change. Developers and designers can load stable mock chat sessions for future Control UI visual review.

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

Restart the gateway to load plugins.

{
  "diagnostics": [],

  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"

      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.

- Fresh open-PR recall found Gmail watcher PRs for delivery mode, OAuth failure handling, secret argv handling, and bind diagnostics, but no PR implementing this single-flight renewal invariant.

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

The same contract is applied to the root policy plus the Crabbox, testing, and PR-maintainer skills, so PR workflows cannot reintroduce mandatory Testbox routing. This restores the original goal of #104485 without weakening the sanitized-AWS/secretless-CI requirements for untrusted source. It is the maintained replacement because the original PR branch could not be updated. Original contributor: @hxy91819.

## User Impact

Operators can set a machine-local preference such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container` without changing the shared skill. AWS or another eligible provider can be selected the same way. Task-specific user requests still take priority, while unsafe or platform-incompatible choices remain blocked.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.


Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```

```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:


Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`
